citations.document_title: Instruction on Christian freedom and liberation – Libertatis conscientia

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly emphasizes freedom, prayer, and the need for man to freely respond to God, but the important claim that the manner of conception causes lasting spiritual enslavement is not supported by the provided sources. It also depicts the possibility of conversion of a person who perseveres in sin in an overly categorical manner: Christian freedom does not exclude the action of God's grace or the power of prayer for another.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic framework holds together God's initiative and human freedom: Christ frees from the slavery of sin, and man accepts this grace and cooperates with it. Therefore, prayer for one's neighbor is meaningful, while its fruits cannot be reduced to a mechanical formula nor can the possibility of later conversion be excluded.
concerns_en: The claim that a spirit associated with adultery or another improper act of conception follows the child and later causes sin is not grounded in the provided sources; such a causal connection can wrongly attribute to the child a spiritual consequence of the parents' sin.

Fasting and prayer can be forms of intercession, but the passage should not present deliverance as a predictable outcome under a certain condition, namely as something that holds only if the person resists on their own.

The claim that no one can change a person who consciously perseveres overlooks that God's grace appeals to freedom and that Christian life is spiritual warfare; freedom does not mean that conversion is no longer possible.

The claim that no one can be saved unless they love God with their heart should be balanced with the teaching that salvation is a gift of grace that man accepts through faith, hope, and love, rather than the result of independent human achievement.

The description of Christianity as a non-coercive religion can be accepted, but the comparison by which it is generally distinguished from other religions is a broad claim that the provided sources do not substantiate.

sections.subtitle_en: When prayer delivers, and when one must wait
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar distinguishes an enslaved person who resists sin from one who has chosen evil
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then distinguishes two types of situations. The first is when a person is **enslaved, but does not want it and resists**. As an example, he mentions a child conceived in adultery or in some other improper manner. The spirit under which they were conceived, he explains, accompanies that child even into adulthood. The person then sins under a power stronger than themselves, for instance entering into a relationship they should not enter. When the father, mother, brother, or sister learns of this, they can **deliver them through fasting and prayer**. The condition is that the person themselves also resists it. Then, he says, prayers are fruitful.

The other situation is when someone has **consciously decided to live that way, defends it, and perseveres in it**. Then, in Grebenar's words, no one can change them. What remains for the family member is to offer them up at Masses and in prayers, be patient, and wait.

He concludes that household members, brothers, sisters, and others have free will and can choose darkness instead of light, and God will not stop them from doing so. God the Father will not take away the gift of free will from any human being. He also points out that no one can enter heaven or be saved who does not love God with their heart and work for the kingdom of God. **Christianity, he conveys, is not a religion of force**, but a revealed truth believed in with the heart and free will, and in this it differs from other religions.

sections.subtitle: Obrezanje srca: bolan put unutarnjeg pročišćenja
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava zašto je obrezanje srca bolno
sections.content:
Grebenar spominje da je o istoj temi govorio i na jednom nedavnom skupu: **koliko boli obrezanje srca**. Obrezanje srca definira kao promjenu srca i nutrine. Tko je prošao proces unutarnjeg pročišćenja, kaže, zna koliko je on bolan.

Objašnjava zašto Stari zavjet za to uzima obredni primjer **tjelesnog obrezanja**. Židovski dječaci obrezivani su osmi dan, pa tako i Isus. Malo dijete ne može riječima izreći koliko ga boli, može samo zaplakati i od straha brzo zaspati. Odrasli koji su prošli taj zahvat svjedočili su da jako boli. Obilježja tog čina su, sažima Grebenar, **bol i krv**.

Podsjeća da sveti Pavao uči kako tjelesno obrezanje samo po sebi ništa ne znači, nego treba obrezati srce. U tome Grebenar vidi i drugu poruku: obrezanje srca jednako boli.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno razumije obrezanje srca kao unutarnju promjenu i uklanjanje onoga što čovjeka odvaja od Boga; Pavao doista suprotstavlja puko oslanjanje na tjelesni znak vjeri koja djeluje ljubavlju. Ipak, tvrdnja da obrezanje srca po svojoj biti jednako boli previše je siguran zaključak iz tjelesne usporedbe: biblijski naglasak je na obraćenju, ljubavi i Božjem djelovanju, a ne na nužnoj emocionalnoj ili tjelesnoj boli.
concerns: Tjelesno obrezanje nije bilo tek primjer boli i krvi nego znak pripadnosti savezu; zato ga nije dobro svesti na obilježja zahvata.

Pavlova tvrdnja da tjelesno obrezanje samo po sebi ne opravdava ne znači da ono nema nikakvo značenje u biblijskom kontekstu; u Kristu spasenje se ne temelji na tom obredu, nego na vjeri koja djeluje ljubavlju.

Ponuđeni izvori ne potvrđuju da je unutarnje pročišćenje nužno jednako bolno kao tjelesni zahvat, ni detalje o djetetovu strahu i uspavljivanju; te dijelove treba predstaviti kao ilustraciju ili osobni dojam, a ne kao biblijski nauk.
magisterium.enrichment: Biblijsko obrezanje srca označava uklanjanje poroka i obnovu nutrine, a ne ponavljanje tjelesnog obreda u duhovnom obliku. Pismo istodobno poziva čovjeka da se obrati i govori o Božjem djelovanju koje omogućuje ljubav prema Bogu; zato pročišćenje može biti teško, ali njegova bit nije bol nego preobrazba srca i vjernost Bogu.

citations.document_title: “What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly understands circumcision of the heart as an inner change and the removal of what separates man from God; Paul indeed contrasts mere reliance on a bodily sign with faith working through love. Nevertheless, the claim that circumcision of the heart essentially hurts just as much is an overly confident conclusion from a physical comparison: the biblical emphasis is on conversion, love, and God's action, rather than on necessary emotional or physical pain.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Biblical circumcision of the heart signifies the removal of vices and the renewal of the interior, rather than the repetition of a physical ritual in spiritual form. Scripture simultaneously calls man to repent and speaks of God's action that makes love of God possible; therefore purification may be difficult, but its essence is not pain but transformation of the heart and fidelity to God.
concerns_en: Bodily circumcision was not merely an example of pain and blood, but a sign of belonging to the covenant; therefore it is not good to reduce it to features of an operation.

Paul's assertion that bodily circumcision does not justify in itself does not mean that it has no meaning in the biblical context; in Christ salvation is not based on that rite, but on faith working through love.

The provided sources do not confirm that inner purification is necessarily just as painful as a physical procedure, nor the details about the child's fear and putting to sleep; these parts should be presented as an illustration or personal impression, rather than biblical teaching.

sections.subtitle_en: Circumcision of the heart: a painful path of interior purification
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host explains why circumcision of the heart is painful
sections.content_en:
Grebenar mentions that he spoke on the same topic at a recent gathering: **how much circumcision of the heart hurts**. He defines circumcision of the heart as a change of heart and inner self. Whoever has undergone the process of interior purification, he says, knows how painful it is.

He explains why the Old Testament takes the ritual example of **physical circumcision** for this. Jewish baby boys were circumcised on the eighth day, and so was Jesus. A small child cannot express in words how much it hurts; it can only cry and quickly fall asleep from fear. Adults who have undergone that procedure have testified that it hurts immensely. The hallmarks of that act, Grebenar summarizes, are **pain and blood**.

He recalls that Saint Paul teaches that physical circumcision in itself means nothing, but rather that the heart must be circumcised. In that, Grebenar sees another message as well: circumcision of the heart hurts just as much.

sections.subtitle: Post kao obrezanje iznutra: „Lagan sam kao ptica“
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar svjedoči o vlastitom iskustvu dugotrajnog posta
sections.content:
Kao praktičan primjer obrezanja srca Grebenar navodi upravo završeni post. Onaj tko posti, kaže, **razapinje svoje tijelo** i klanja se Isusu Kristu. Post boli i tjelesna je bol, ali donosi milost i plodove. Nabraja što ljudi koji poste doživljavaju:

- oslobađaju se grešnih navika i poroka,
- ozdravljaju,
- netko se u obitelji obrati,
- mijenjaju se životne okolnosti,
- postaju strpljiviji i radosniji.

Iznosi i osobno iskustvo. Kada dugotrajno posti, osjeća se **„lagan kao ptica“**: treba mu manje sna, tijelo mu je spremnije i poletniji je. Post ga, kaže, čisti i obrezuje iznutra. Što je pala ljudska narav više pobijeđena i „komprimirana“, to je više milosti u čovjeku i to snažnije djeluje Duh Sveti.

Odatle izvodi razliku između **ljudi duha i ljudi tijela**. Ljudi duha vole postiti jer im je tako duh slobodniji. Ljudi tijela ne mogu postiti jer misle samo na dobar obrok. Kada dođe post, kaže, „mazne ribu“ pa sami sebe lažu da poste. Mnogi, tvrdi, ne poste ni na Čistu srijedu i Veliki petak, dva dana koja propisuje Crkva.

Na pitanje zašto neki ne mogu postiti odgovara da ne žele vršiti volju Božju. Kada je čovjek zaokupljen pitanjem što je Božja volja, Bog mu pritječe u pomoć i tada „sve može u onome koji ga jača“, jer Bog ide s onima koji idu za njim.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno ističe da post može služiti obraćenju, unutarnjem čišćenju, poslušnosti Bogu i rastu u molitvi, ali neke tvrdnje pretjeruju i mogu stvoriti pogrešan dojam da je tjelesno „komprimiranje” samo po sebi mjerilo milosti. Također nije opravdano iz nemogućnosti ili neprakticiranja posta zaključiti da osoba ne želi Božju volju.
concerns: Post je sredstvo kršćanskog života, a ne način stjecanja ili mjerenja milosti: crkveni tekst ga povezuje s unutarnjim obraćenjem i ljubavlju, ali naglašava da nije „glavno dobro” samo po sebi.

Tvrdnja da više „pobijeđena” ili „komprimirana” ljudska narav znači više milosti nije dobro uravnotežena; post treba voditi slobodi od grijeha i ljubavi, a ne preziru prema tijelu ili pretpostavci da je tjelesna patnja sama po sebi duhovna korist.

Oslobađanje od poroka, ozdravljenje, obraćenje člana obitelji ili promjena okolnosti mogu se dogoditi, ali ne treba ih predstavljati kao očekivane ili zajamčene plodove posta; izvori naglašavaju molitvu, obraćenje i djelotvornu ljubav, a ne obećanje takvih ishoda.
Crkveno učenje povezuje post s poslušnošću Božjoj volji, ali iz toga ne slijedi da svatko tko ne posti ne želi Božju volju: mogu postojati opravdane zapreke, uključujući zdravlje i dob.
Treba razlikovati post od nemrsa: crkveni tekst izričito navodi i post i uzdržavanje od mesa kao različite obveze, pa jedenje ribe samo po sebi ne znači da osoba ne posti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje posta spaja vanjsko odricanje s unutarnjim obraćenjem, molitvom i brigom za bližnjega; post nije cilj sam sebi, nego sredstvo koje treba oblikovati ljubav i poslušnost Bogu. Zato se osobno iskustvo veće poletnosti može iznijeti kao svjedočanstvo, ali ne kao opće pravilo ni dokaz posebne razine milosti.

citations.document_title: General Audience of 5 March 2003, Ash Wednesday

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly emphasizes that fasting can serve conversion, inner cleansing, obedience to God, and growth in prayer, but some claims exaggerate and can create the mistaken impression that physical "compression" is in itself a measure of grace. It is also not justified to conclude from the inability or non-practice of fasting that a person does not want God's will.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of fasting combines external renunciation with inner conversion, prayer, and care for one's neighbor; fasting is not an end in itself, but a means that should shape love and obedience to God. Therefore, the personal experience of greater enthusiasm can be presented as a testimony, but not as a general rule or proof of a special level of grace.
concerns_en: Fasting is a means of Christian life, rather than a way of acquiring or measuring grace: Church texts connect it with inner conversion and love, but emphasize that it is not the "chief good" in itself.

The claim that more "conquered" or "compressed" human nature means more grace is not well balanced; fasting should lead to freedom from sin and to love, rather than to contempt for the body or the assumption that physical suffering is in itself a spiritual benefit.

Deliverance from vices, healing, conversion of a family member, or change of circumstances can happen, but they should not be presented as expected or guaranteed fruits of fasting; sources emphasize prayer, conversion, and effective love, rather than the promise of such outcomes.

Church teaching connects fasting with obedience to God's will, but from this it does not follow that everyone who does not fast does not want God's will: there may be justified impediments, including health and age.

One must distinguish fasting from abstinence: Church texts explicitly cite both fasting and abstinence from meat as distinct obligations, so eating fish in itself does not mean that a person is not fasting.

sections.subtitle_en: Fasting as circumcision from within: “I am light as a bird”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar testifies about his own experience of long-term fasting
sections.content_en:
As a practical example of circumcision of the heart, Grebenar cites the just-completed fast. Whoever fasts, he says, **crucifies their flesh** and adores Jesus Christ. Fasting hurts and is bodily pain, but it brings grace and fruits. He enumerates what people who fast experience:

- they are freed from sinful habits and vices,
- they are healed,
- someone in the family converts,
- life circumstances change,
- they become more patient and joyful.

He also shares a personal experience. When he fasts for a prolonged period, he feels **“light as a bird”**: he needs less sleep, his body is readier, and he is more spirited. Fasting, he says, cleanses and circumcises him from within. The more fallen human nature is conquered and "compressed", the more grace there is in man and the more powerfully the Holy Spirit acts.

From this he derives the distinction between **people of the spirit and people of the flesh**. People of the spirit love to fast because their spirit is freer that way. People of the flesh cannot fast because they only think about a good meal. When fasting comes, he says, they "snatch fish" and lie to themselves that they are fasting. Many, he asserts, do not even fast on Ash Wednesday and Good Friday, the two days prescribed by the Church.

To the question of why some cannot fast, he replies that they do not want to do God's will. When a person is preoccupied with what God's will is, God comes to their aid and then "they can do all things through Him who strengthens them", because God goes with those who follow Him.
keywords_en: people of the spirit and people of the flesh

sections.subtitle: Farizejska vjera i Božja zaštita na prvoj crti
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o prepoznavanju duhovne tame
sections.content:
Suprotnost obrezanom srcu Grebenar vidi u **farizejskoj vjeri**: vjerovanju „tradicionalno“, kroz folklor, običaj i hrvatstvo. Takvi ljudi, kaže, lažu sami sebe da su vjernici, a ništa se ne događa. Vjera i Crkva postaju im tek sredstvo za umirivanje savjesti. Više ih zanimaju politika i svjetovnost, druže se sa svima i svakim, a to pokazuje da im srce nije obrezano.

Obrezano srce i pročišćena nutrina, tumači, omogućuju čovjeku da **vidi duhovnu tamu oko sebe**. Takav čovjek ne ide tamo gdje je tama, osim ako ga Bog ne šalje. Poziva se na psalam: „Da mi je dolinom smrti proći, zla se ne bojim.“ Postoje, kaže, i geografska područja na kojima je tama velika.

No upravo ondje gdje je tama najveća, Bog izlijeva još veću milost na one koji vrše njegovu volju. Isus se, naglašava Grebenar, **ne povlači s prve linije**. On želi razoriti i razotkriti djela tame, pa onoga tko ondje vrši Božju volju posebno štiti. Izaijin tekst o tami koja zastire narode tumači kao sliku **rata u nebu između anđela svjetla i anđela tame**, koji se bore za to kakvo će duhovno nebo biti nad ljudima.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak sadrži legitimno upozorenje da običaj i nacionalni identitet sami po sebi nisu isto što i živa vjera te da je kršćanski život obilježen duhovnom borbom. Međutim, široko osuđivanje ljudi na temelju njihova druženja ili političkih interesa, kao i prikaz Božje zaštite na „prvoj crti” kao posebnog jamstva, prelaze ono što se može sigurno zaključiti iz vjere i navedenih biblijskih slika.
concerns: Nazvati vjeru „farizejskom” samo zato što je tradicionalna ili povezana s običajem, hrvatstvom ili politikom preširoka je osuda: problem je licemjerje ili svođenje vjere na vanjski identitet, a ne tradicija ili kulturna pripadnost same po sebi.

Tvrdnja da druženje sa „svima i svakim” pokazuje neobraćeno srce ne uzima u obzir kršćanski poziv na ljubav prema ljudima i razborito razlučivanje; iz opisanih ponašanja ne može se pouzdano suditi o nečijoj nutrini.

Psalam o prolasku dolinom smrti izražava pouzdanje u Boga, ali ne daje osnovu za obećanje da će Bog posebno zaštititi svakoga tko se nađe u opasnosti ili da vjernik treba tražiti opasna područja. Oprez i izbjegavanje zla mogu biti razboriti; zaštita ne znači nužno tjelesnu sigurnost.

Prikaz Izaijine slike tame nad narodima kao određenog rata između anđela svjetla i tame može biti duhovno tumačenje, ali dostupni tekstovi ne potvrđuju da je to jedino ili izravno značenje toga odlomka, niti da se radi o geografskim područjima s osobito velikom tamom.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska tradicija govori o stvarnoj duhovnoj borbi, ali njezino razumijevanje ne opravdava senzacionalizam ni sigurne tvrdnje o nevidljivim silama u pojedinim područjima; potiče na vjernost, razboritost i pouzdanje u Boga. Primjer mudraca koji izbjegavaju Herodovu palaču pokazuje da čuvanje vjere može uključivati razborito udaljavanje od opasnosti, a ne nužno ostajanje na „prvoj crti”.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage contains a legitimate warning that custom and national identity in themselves are not the same as living faith and that Christian life is marked by spiritual warfare. However, broad condemnation of people based on their socializing or political interests, as well as the presentation of God's protection on the "front line" as a special guarantee, exceed what can be safely concluded from faith and the cited biblical images.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian tradition speaks of real spiritual warfare, but its understanding does not justify sensationalism or certain claims about invisible forces in individual areas; it encourages fidelity, prudence, and trust in God. The example of the magi avoiding Herod's palace shows that guarding faith can include a prudent distance from danger, and not necessarily remaining on the "front line."
concerns_en: Calling faith "Pharisaic" solely because it is traditional or connected with custom, Croatian identity, or politics is too broad a condemnation: the problem is hypocrisy or reducing faith to an external identity, rather than tradition or cultural belonging in themselves.

The claim that socializing with "anyone and everyone" shows an unconverted heart does not take into account the Christian call to love people and exercise prudent discernment; one cannot reliably judge someone's interior from the described behaviors.

The psalm about walking through the valley of death expresses trust in God, but does not provide a basis for the promise that God will specially protect anyone who finds themselves in danger or that a believer should seek out dangerous areas. Caution and avoiding evil can be prudent; protection does not necessarily mean physical safety.

Presenting Isaiah's image of darkness over the nations as a specific war between angels of light and darkness may be a spiritual interpretation, but the available texts do not confirm that this is the sole or direct meaning of that passage, nor that it involves geographical areas with particularly great darkness.

sections.subtitle_en: Pharisaic faith and God's protection on the front line
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host speaks about recognizing spiritual darkness
sections.content_en:
Grebenar sees the opposite of a circumcised heart in **Pharisaic faith**: believing "traditionally", through folklore, custom, and Croathood. Such people, he says, lie to themselves that they are believers, yet nothing happens. Faith and the Church become merely a means to soothe their conscience. They are more interested in politics and worldliness, mingle with anyone and everyone, and that shows their heart is not circumcised.

A circumcised heart and a purified interior, he explains, enable a person to **see the spiritual darkness around them**. Such a person does not go where darkness is, unless God sends them. He refers to the psalm: "Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I fear no evil." There are also, he says, geographical regions where darkness is great.

Yet precisely where darkness is greatest, God pours out even greater grace upon those who do His will. Jesus, Grebenar emphasizes, **does not retreat from the front line**. He wants to destroy and expose the deeds of darkness, so He especially protects whoever does God's will there. He interprets Isaiah's text about the darkness covering the nations as an image of the **war in heaven between angels of light and angels of darkness**, fighting over what kind of spiritual heaven will be over the people.

sections.subtitle: Obrezanje naroda: Europa, pobačaj i prosvjedi u Francuskoj
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar govori o Europi koja više voli pobačaj od života
sections.content:
Iz osobne razine Grebenar prelazi na zajedničku: **kao što pojedinac treba obrezati srce, mora se dogoditi i obrezanje naroda**, a ono je uvijek bolno. Do toga dolazi, objašnjava, kada narod zastrani, odnosno kada većina pojedinaca u njemu više ljubi zlo i grijeh.

Kao primjer navodi narode nekad kršćanske Europe. Oni, kaže, više vole pobačaj nego život i više im je stalo do prava na ubojstvo djeteta nego do njegova rođenja. Posebno izdvaja Francusku, gdje je predsjednik Macron zatražio da se pravo na pobačaj unese u ustav. To naziva djelom bolesnih umova, a francuskog predsjednika oštro uspoređuje s „Hitlerom i Herodom ovog vremena“.

Osvrće se zatim na **prosvjede u Francuskoj i Belgiji**. Strani komentatori i analitičari, kaže, pitaju tko stoji iza njih i ne znaju odgovoriti. Grebenar odgovara da iza toga stoji sam Sotona i da nije potrebna nikakva organizacija. Opisuje što vidi na ulicama:

- mladi Francuzi izlaze zajedno s djecom migranata,
- nema francuskih zastava, nose se palestinske,
- nije jasno zašto prosvjeduju, navodno za bolje školstvo,
- mete su trgovine, obrti, OPG-ovi, mikropoduzeća i obiteljske radnje koje razaraju.

Razlog tome vidi u **duhu komunizma i socijalizma**, koji po njegovu tumačenju ide zajedno s duhom islama. Kao primjer navodi Bosnu i Hercegovinu, gdje, kaže, Bošnjaci jako žale za socijalizmom i tim vremenima.

magisterium.assessment: Osuda pobačaja i obrana nerođenog života u skladu su s katoličkim naukom: Crkva naučava da se zapovijed „Ne ubij” odnosi i na nerođeno dijete te pobačaj smatra teškim moralnim zlom. Međutim, proglašavanje Sotone uzrokom prosvjeda, povezivanje islama sa socijalizmom i usporedba Macrona s Hitlerom i Herodom iznose se kao teološke ili moralne tvrdnje bez odgovarajućeg temelja te zamagljuju razliku između obrane života i političke polemike.
concerns: „Obrezanje naroda” može poslužiti kao propovjednička metafora, ali prikazivanje narodnog stradanja kao nužnog ili Božjeg odgovora na to što je većina navodno zavoljela grijeh nije u priloženom materijalu utemeljeno kao katolički nauk.

Tvrdnja da iza prosvjeda stoji Sotona iznosi se kao sigurnost, premda se iz dostupnih podataka ne može utvrditi nadnaravni uzrok političkih događaja; time se složene društvene okolnosti zamjenjuju nedokazanom tvrdnjom.
Povezivanje islama i socijalizma te široke tvrdnje o Francuzima, Belgijancima ili Bošnjacima nedovoljno su obrazložene i mogu nepravedno pripisati kolektivnu krivnju ili motive čitavim skupinama.
Usporedba živućeg političkog vođe s Hitlerom i Herodom retorički je zapaljiva i nije potrebna za jasno iznošenje katoličkog protivljenja pobačaju.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička osuda pobačaja temelji se na dostojanstvu ljudskog života od njegova početka, a ne na političkoj pripadnosti ili nacionalnoj krivnji; Ivan Pavao II. ističe da Sveto pismo ne govori izravno i posebno o namjernom pobačaju, ali njegovo poštovanje života u majčinoj utrobi podupire primjenu zapovijedi „Ne ubij” i na nerođeno dijete. Zato se protivljenje nepravednom zakonu može i treba obrazlagati argumentima o zaštiti života i općem dobru, bez pripisivanja nadnaravnih motiva prosvjednicima ili demoniziranja političkih protivnika.

magisterium.assessment_en: The condemnation of abortion and defense of unborn life are in accordance with Catholic teaching: the Church teaches that the commandment "Thou shalt not kill" also applies to the unborn child and considers abortion a grave moral evil. However, declaring Satan the cause of protests, linking Islam with socialism, and comparing Macron to Hitler and Herod are presented as theological or moral claims without adequate foundation and blur the distinction between defense of life and political polemic.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic condemnation of abortion is based on the dignity of human life from its beginning, rather than on political affiliation or national guilt; John Paul II emphasizes that Sacred Scripture does not speak directly and specifically about intentional abortion, but its respect for life in the mother's womb supports the application of the commandment "Thou shalt not kill" to the unborn child as well. Therefore, opposition to an unjust law can and must be argued with points on the protection of life and the common good, without attributing supernatural motives to protesters or demonizing political opponents.
concerns_en: "Circumcision of the nation" can serve as a homiletic metaphor, but presenting national suffering as necessary or as God's response to the fact that the majority supposedly grew fond of sin is not grounded in the attached material as Catholic teaching.

The claim that Satan is behind the protests is presented as a certainty, although from the available data one cannot establish a supernatural cause of political events; through this, complex social circumstances are replaced by an unproven claim.
Linking Islam and socialism as well as broad claims about the French, Belgians, or Bosniaks are insufficiently explained and can unjustly attribute collective guilt or motives to entire groups.
Comparing a living political leader to Hitler and Herod is rhetorically inflammatory and not necessary for clearly presenting Catholic opposition to abortion.

sections.subtitle_en: Circumcision of the nation: Europe, abortion, and protests in France
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar speaks about Europe loving abortion more than life
sections.content_en:
From the personal level, Grebenar moves to the collective: **just as an individual needs to circumcise their heart, the circumcision of a nation must also take place**, and it is always painful. This occurs, he explains, when a nation goes astray, namely when the majority of individuals in it love evil and sin more.

As an example, he mentions the nations of once Christian Europe. They, he says, love abortion more than life and care more about the right to kill a child than about its birth. He singles out France in particular, where President Macron demanded that the right to abortion be enshrined in the constitution. He calls that the work of sick minds, and harshly compares the French president to "the Hitler and Herod of our time".

He then reflects on the **protests in France and Belgium**. Foreign commentators and analysts, he says, ask who is behind them and cannot answer. Grebenar answers that behind it stands Satan himself and that no organization is needed. He describes what he sees on the streets:

- young French people go out together with children of migrants,
- there are no French flags, Palestinian ones are carried,
- it is not clear why they are protesting, ostensibly for better education,
- the targets are shops, trade crafts, family farms (OPGs), micro-enterprises, and family workshops, which they destroy.

He sees the reason for this in the **spirit of communism and socialism**, which in his interpretation goes hand in hand with the spirit of Islam. As an example, he cites Bosnia and Herzegovina, where, he says, Bosniaks deeply grieve for socialism and those times.

sections.subtitle: Generacija Z: odgojena da ne preuzima odgovornost
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj kritizira školski odgoj mladih generacija
sections.content:
Zašto su privatne trgovine i poduzeća postali meta europske mladeži? Grebenar odgovara da je Europa odgojila **generaciju Z** tako da prihvati komunizam, odnosno da bude **nesposobna preuzeti odgovornost** za sebe, svoju obitelj i domovinu.

Krivnju pripisuje školskom sustavu. Djecu se, kaže, uči da su homoseksualizam, koji naziva sodomijom, i pobačaj nešto dobro, a u to vjeruju i mnogi mladi učitelji, „gotovo opsjednuti“ time. Tvrdi da mnogi od njih imaju raspadnute brakove ili ne zasnivaju obitelj, a neki nakon takvih predbračnih života ne mogu imati djece. Za sebe kaže da govori o nečemu što zna. Dodaje da toga možda manje ima u Hercegovini, ali u Hrvatskoj itekako. Roditelji pritom nisu svjesni što se događa, a dijete više vremena provede u školi nego kod kuće.

Posljedicu sažima pitanjem: ako mlada osoba nije sposobna preuzeti odgovornost za vlastitu budućnost, kako će preuzeti odgovornost za budućnost naroda? Takvi mladi traže da im **država riješi probleme**, a malo tko se pita koja je njegova vlastita uloga u društvu.

Poruku upućuje i francuskim prosvjednicima, među kojima su mladi, učitelji i sindikati: Macrona i njegovu vladu sami su birali. Francuski kršćani i katolici šutjeli su, kaže, dok je vlada odobravala pobačaj, istospolne zajednice i migrantsku politiku, a isto se, tvrdi, događa i u Hrvatskoj. Kada katolici šute, sustav im odgaja djecu. Takav duh, koji ne podnosi poduzetništvo ni obiteljski posao, naziva **duhom socijalizma i duhom antikrista**.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na odgovorno kršćansko sudjelovanje u odgoju i društvu te odbacivanje pobačaja i istospolnih spolnih čina može se osloniti na katolički nauk, ali način izlaganja sadrži ozbiljne neutemeljene generalizacije o mladima, učiteljima, njihovim brakovima i plodnosti. Navođenje političkih stavova i ponašanja cijelih skupina kao „duha antikrista”, uz nedovoljno razlikovanje osobe, čina i ideologije, nije uravnotežena ni dostatno potkrijepljena teološka prosudba.
concerns: Tvrdnje da je generacija Z odgojena da prihvati komunizam ili da mladi nisu sposobni preuzeti odgovornost iznose se kao široke činjenice bez potpore u priloženim izvorima.
Tvrdnje da učitelji imaju raspadnute brakove ili ne mogu imati djecu zbog predbračnog života nisu potkrijepljene teologijom navedenom ovdje i mogu nepravedno stigmatizirati osobe.

Katolički nauk razlikuje objektivnu moralnu prosudbu spolnih čina od dostojanstva i osobne krivnje pojedinaca; govor o homoseksualnosti kao „sodomiji” bez te razlike riskira poistovjećivanje osobe s činom i zanemarivanje poziva na poštovanje.
Oznaka „duh antikrista” primijenjena na široke političke ili gospodarske stavove nije obrazložena, a ne pruža dovoljno preciznu moralnu analizu konkretnih postupaka ili politika.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk smatra da istospolni spolni čini ne odgovaraju moralnom redu, ali istodobno zahtijeva da se osobe homoseksualnih sklonosti prihvaćaju s poštovanjem i bez nepravedne diskriminacije; objektivna prosudba čina sama po sebi ne određuje osobnu krivnju. Katolički odgoj mladih uključuje oblikovanje za svetost, odgovornost i služenje, no to ne opravdava pripisivanje istih uvjerenja ili mana čitavoj generaciji.

citations.document_author: Catholic Bishops’ Conference of England and Wales

magisterium.assessment_en: The call for responsible Christian participation in education and society and the rejection of abortion and same-sex sexual acts can rely on Catholic teaching, but the manner of presentation contains serious unfounded generalizations about youth, teachers, their marriages, and fertility. Citing political views and behaviors of entire groups as the "spirit of the Antichrist," along with insufficient distinction between person, act, and ideology, is neither a balanced nor a sufficiently supported theological judgment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching holds that same-sex sexual acts do not correspond to the moral order, but at the same time requires that persons with homosexual tendencies be accepted with respect and without unjust discrimination; objective judgment of the act in itself does not determine personal guilt. Catholic education of youth includes formation for holiness, responsibility, and service, but that does not justify attributing the same beliefs or flaws to an entire generation.
concerns_en: Claims that Generation Z was raised to accept communism or that youth are unable to take responsibility are presented as broad facts without support in the attached sources.
Claims that teachers have broken marriages or cannot have children because of premarital life are not supported by the theology cited here and can unjustly stigmatize persons.

Catholic teaching distinguishes the objective moral judgment of sexual acts from the dignity and personal guilt of individuals; speaking of homosexuality as "sodomy" without that distinction risks equating the person with the act and neglecting the call to respect.
The label "spirit of the Antichrist" applied to broad political or economic stances is not substantiated, and does not provide a sufficiently precise moral analysis of concrete actions or policies.

sections.subtitle_en: Generation Z: raised not to take responsibility
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host criticizes the school education of young generations
sections.content_en:
Why have private stores and businesses become the target of European youth? Grebenar answers that Europe has raised **Generation Z** to embrace communism, that is, to be **incapable of taking responsibility** for themselves, their families, and their homeland.

He places the blame on the school system. Children, he says, are taught that homosexuality, which he calls sodomy, and abortion are something good, and many young teachers, "almost obsessed" with it, believe this as well. He claims that many of them have broken marriages or do not start families, and some, after such premarital lifestyles, cannot have children. Regarding himself, he says he speaks of something he knows. He adds that there may be less of this in Hercegovina, but in Croatia very much so. Parents, meanwhile, are not aware of what is happening, and a child spends more time at school than at home.

He summarizes the consequence with a question: if a young person is not capable of taking responsibility for their own future, how will they take responsibility for the future of the nation? Such young people demand that **the state solve their problems**, and hardly anyone asks what their own role in society is.

He also directs a message to the French protesters, including youth, teachers, and unions: they elected Macron and his government themselves. French Christians and Catholics remained silent, he says, while the government approved abortion, same-sex civil unions, and migrant policy, and the same, he claims, is happening in Croatia. When Catholics remain silent, the system raises their children. Such a spirit, which cannot stand entrepreneurship or family business, he calls the **spirit of socialism and the spirit of the antichrist**.

sections.subtitle: Povratak komunizma: od faraonova Egipta do Isusa tesara
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar uspoređuje komunizam s egipatskim ropstvom Izraelaca
sections.content:
Grebenar povezuje te pojave s Izaijinim pokrivačem. Danas je, kaže, u Europi i zapadnom svijetu na djelu **povratak komunizma**, tamnog prekrivača koji je nekad pokrivao istočni blok iza željezne zavjese. Oni njegovih godina i stariji, dodaje, toga se dobro sjećaju.

Komunizam definira kao stanje u kojem **država odlučuje što će čovjek raditi**. Prvu komunističku, socijalističku ekonomiju pronalazi u **Egiptu**: Izraelci su bili radnici, a Egipćani „članovi partije“ faraonova naroda. Faraon je imao jednu jedinu stranku i svi su radili za njega. Današnji povratak komunizma vidi kao sofisticiraniji i učinkovitiji od onoga nekad. U pozivima na prosvjede u Hrvatskoj u ime marksizma vidi djelo samog Sotone: mlade se poziva da mrze poduzetništvo i neovisnost te da država sve uzme i jednako raspodijeli.

Takvoj „socijalnoj pravdi“ suprotstavlja **Isusove kriterije**: „Komu je dano, njemu će se dati još više da obiluje, a tko misli da nešto ima, oduzet će mu se.“ Tumači da će Isus dati sve potrebno, i materijalno, onome tko širi kraljevstvo Božje.

Posebno naglašava da je **Krist bio poduzetan**. Trideset godina bio je tesar koji je svojim rukama stvarao, najprije uz svetog Josipa, a nakon Josipove smrti i sam. Isus i Josip imali su svoj posao, bili su neovisni i poduzetni. Grebenar dodaje da nije problem raditi kod drugoga, ali takvi poslovi čekaju one kojima su namijenjeni.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ima katolički prihvatljivu jezgru u obrani osobne inicijative i upozorenju na prisilnu državnu kontrolu, ali nauk Crkve istodobno traži da se privatno vlasništvo i gospodarska djelatnost usmjeravaju prema općem dobru, a ne svode na suprotnost između države i poduzetništva. Pojedine tvrdnje pretjerano pojednostavljuju političku i biblijsku temu, osobito poistovjećivanjem faraonova Egipta s komunizmom i tumačenjem Isusovih riječi kao obećanja materijalnog obilja.
concerns: Opis faraonova Egipta kao prve komunističke ekonomije anakronistička je politička analogija, a ne utemeljeno tumačenje biblijskog izvještaja.

Prispodoba o tome da će se onome komu je dano dati još više govori o odgovornom prihvaćanju i umnažanju povjerenih darova; iz nje se ne može zaključiti da će Krist poduzetnoj osobi osigurati materijalni uspjeh.

Pripisivanje političkih prosvjeda djelovanju Sotone bez razlučivanja njihovih konkretnih zahtjeva može nepravedno demonizirati političke protivnike; katolički pristup javnom životu uključuje dijalog i odbacivanje gorčine i klevete.
Isusov rad tesara može biti primjer dostojanstva ljudskog rada, ali sam po sebi ne dokazuje da je Krist promicao poduzetništvo ili ekonomsku neovisnost kao kršćanski ideal.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički socijalni nauk ne poistovjećuje pravednost s državnim upravljanjem svim radom niti s neograničenim individualizmom: pravo na vlasništvo postoji, ali se njegova uporaba prosuđuje prema odgovornosti prema bližnjemu i općem dobru. Isusov primjer rada može nadahnuti poštovanje prema poštenom radu i odgovornosti, no ne treba ga pretvarati u potvrdu jedne gospodarske politike ili u jamstvo osobnog bogatstva.

citations.document_title: Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship: A Call to Political Responsibility from the Catholic Bishops of the United States with New Introductory Note
citations.document_author: United States Conference of Catholic Bishops

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage has a Catholically acceptable core in defending personal initiative and warning against coercive state control, but the Church's teaching at the same time requires that private property and economic activity be directed toward the common good, rather than reduced to an opposition between the state and entrepreneurship. Certain claims overly simplify the political and biblical theme, especially by equating Pharaoh's Egypt with communism and interpreting Jesus' words as a promise of material abundance.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic social teaching does not equate justice with state management of all labor nor with unlimited individualism: the right to property exists, but its use is judged according to responsibility toward one's neighbor and the common good. Jesus' example of labor can inspire respect for honest work and responsibility, but it should not be turned into a confirmation of one economic policy or into a guarantee of personal wealth.
concerns_en: The description of Pharaoh's Egypt as the first communist economy is an anachronistic political analogy, rather than a well-founded interpretation of the biblical account.

The parable that to anyone who has will more be given speaks of the responsible acceptance and multiplication of entrusted gifts; from it one cannot conclude that Christ will secure material success for an enterprising person.

Attributing political protests to the action of Satan without discerning their concrete demands can unjustly demonize political opponents; a Catholic approach to public life includes dialogue and the rejection of bitterness and slander.
Jesus' work as a carpenter can be an example of the dignity of human labor, but in itself does not prove that Christ promoted entrepreneurship or economic independence as a Christian ideal.

sections.subtitle_en: The return of communism: from Pharaoh's Egypt to Jesus the carpenter
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar compares communism to the Egyptian slavery of the Israelites
sections.content_en:
Grebenar connects these phenomena with Isaiah's veil. Today, he says, in Europe and the Western world, a **return of communism** is at work, a dark covering that once covered the Eastern Bloc behind the Iron Curtain. Those of his age and older, he adds, remember it well.

He defines communism as a state in which **the state decides what a person will do**. He finds the first communist, socialist economy in **Egypt**: the Israelites were workers, and the Egyptians were "party members" of Pharaoh's people. Pharaoh had one single party and everyone worked for him. He views today's return of communism as more sophisticated and effective than the one in the past. In calls for protests in Croatia in the name of Marxism, he sees the work of Satan himself: young people are called upon to hate entrepreneurship and independence and to demand that the state take everything and distribute it equally.

To such "social justice" he contrasts **Jesus' criteria**: "To everyone who has, more will be given and he will have an abundance; but from him who has not, even what he has will be taken away." He explains that Jesus will provide everything necessary, including material things, to whoever spreads the Kingdom of God.

He particularly emphasizes that **Christ was enterprising**. For thirty years He was a carpenter who created with His hands, first alongside Saint Joseph, and after Joseph's death on His own. Jesus and Joseph had their own business, they were independent and enterprising. Grebenar adds that there is no problem working for someone else, but such jobs await those for whom they are intended.

sections.subtitle: Molitva i post samo su jedna strana kovanice
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva obitelji da pokrenu vlastiti posao
sections.content:
Iz primjera Isusa tesara Grebenar izvodi konkretan poziv hrvatskom narodu: **neka mnogo obitelji pokrene vlastiti posao**, obrt, OPG ili mikropoduzeće. Ništa, kaže, nije takav lijek društvu kao malo poduzetništvo koje izrasta iz obitelji. Kada otac i majka rade zajedno, i djeca će sutra tako raditi. Neće, slikovito kaže, „vući načelnika i župana za ruku“ da im zaposle dijete, nego će stvarati vlastitim rukama.

Naglašava da **molitva i post nisu dovoljni**. Uspoređuje ih s kovanicom koja ima pismo i glavu: molitva i post samo su jedna njezina strana. Druga je strana pokretanje inicijativa. Tko nema vlastitu tvrtku, neka bude poduzetan ondje gdje radi, u privatnom ili javnom poduzeću, i pokrene nešto novo.

I time se, poručuje, **razaraju djela tame**. Takav čovjek neće samo kritizirati državu i politiku. Kada sam nešto pokreće, prepoznat će i koga treba birati na izborima, jer će vidjeti koji su ljudi oni koje Bog šalje.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na obiteljsku inicijativu, odgovoran rad i praktično služenje zajednici uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim naukom, joka gospodarsku djelatnost vrednuje prema njezinu doprinosu osobama i općem dobru. Ipak, tvrdnje da je malo poduzetništvo lijek društvu te da se iz osobne inicijative može prepoznati koga Bog šalje na izborima mogu zvučati previše apsolutno i nedovoljno uvažavati razborito prosuđivanje različitih političkih i životnih okolnosti.
concerns: Molitva i post ne smiju se prikazati kao nedostatni sami po sebi: kršćanska je poanta da duhovni život treba donositi plodove u djelima, a ne da se molitva podređuje poduzetništvu.

Malo obiteljsko poduzetništvo može biti vrijedan oblik sudjelovanja u društvu, ali nije jedini katolički odgovor na društvene probleme; Crkva ne propisuje jedan gospodarski model, nego traži razborito prosuđivanje konkretnih okolnosti.
Glasovanje zahtijeva prosudbu kandidata, njihovih stajališta i karaktera; nije opravdano političkog kandidata predstavljati kao osobu koju je Bog sigurno poslao.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje rada povezuje poduzetnost s odgovornošću: obiteljsko poduzeće može služiti zajednici kada vodi računa o radnicima, dugoročnom dobru obitelji i zajedničkom domu, a ne samo o vlastitom uspjehu. Molitva, post i djelovanje nisu suparnici: kršćanska molitva treba oblikovati konkretno zauzimanje za bližnje, dok se političke i gospodarske odluke donose razborito i uz poštovanje dostojanstva svih osoba.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call for family initiative, responsible work, and practical service to the community is largely aligned with Catholic teaching, which evaluates economic activity according to its contribution to persons and the common good. Nevertheless, claims that small entrepreneurship is a cure for society and that from personal initiative one can recognize whom God sends in elections may sound too absolute and insufficiently respect the prudent judgment of different political and life circumstances.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of work connects enterprise with responsibility: a family enterprise can serve the community when it takes into account workers, the long-term good of the family, and the common home, rather than only its own success. Prayer, fasting, and action are not rivals: Christian prayer should shape concrete engagement for one's neighbors, while political and economic decisions are made prudently and with respect for the dignity of all persons.
concerns_en: Prayer and fasting must not be presented as insufficient in themselves: the Christian point is that spiritual life should bear fruit in deeds, not that prayer is subordinated to entrepreneurship.

Small family entrepreneurship can be a valuable form of participation in society, but it is not the only Catholic answer to social problems; the Church does not prescribe a single economic model, but calls for prudent judgment of concrete circumstances.
Voting requires the assessment of candidates, their positions, and character; it is not justified to present a political candidate as a person whom God has certainly sent.

sections.subtitle_en: Prayer and fasting are only one side of the coin
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host calls on families to start their own businesses
sections.content_en:
From the example of Jesus the carpenter, Grebenar draws a concrete appeal to the Croatian people: **let many families start their own business**, craft, family farm (OPG), or micro-enterprise. Nothing, he says, is such a remedy for society as small entrepreneurship that grows out of the family. When father and mother work together, the children will also work that way tomorrow. They will not, as he puts it colorfully, "drag the municipal mayor and county prefect by the arm" to get their child employed, but will create with their own hands.

He emphasizes that **prayer and fasting are not enough**. He compares them to a coin that has heads and tails: prayer and fasting are only one of its sides. The other side is taking initiatives. Whoever does not have their own company should be enterprising where they work, in a private or public company, and initiate something new.

And by this, he conveys, **the works of darkness are destroyed**. Such a person will not merely criticize the state and politics. When they initiate something themselves, they will also recognize whom to vote for in elections, because they will see which people are those whom God sends.

sections.subtitle: Kad narod zastrani: Irska, demokracija i opomena iz Akite
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar navodi irske referendume kao primjer zastranjenja naroda
sections.content:
„Narod može oboljeti“, upozorava Grebenar i tvrdi da **demokracija nije temeljna vrijednost onako kako je Bog vidi**. Kao primjer navodi **Irsku**: irski narod je na dva referenduma izglasao najprije pravo na pobačaj, a zatim pravo istospolnih parova na posvajanje djece. Podsjeća da su se katolici prije dvadesetak godina dičili „katoličkom Irskom“, a ona je, kaže, sama donijela „sotonine zakone“.

Sveto pismo, osobito Stari zavjet, uči da cijeli narod ili njegov veći dio može krenuti krivim smjerom. Kada većina prezre ono što je Božje, Bog dopušta nešto bolno kako bi **obrezao narod**. Usporedbu povlači s pojedincem: tko se ne ponizi pred Bogom postom i sam ne razapne svoje tijelo, toga će Bog poniziti na svoj način kako bi ga popravio.

Ako se narod klanja đavlu i bira ga umjesto Oca nebeskoga, Bog to po Grebenarovu tumačenju pravedno dopušta: onaj kojemu se narod klanja počinje vladati njime. Među takve idole ubraja i **nacionalizam**, pretjeranu ljubav prema zastavi, hrvatstvu, srpstvu ili amerikanizmu, kao u Njemačkoj za vrijeme Hitlera. Đavao, kaže, ne zna vladati nego samo udarati. Tada stradaju i nevini i prolijeva se nevina krv.

Podsjeća na poruku iz **Akite**: ako se čovječanstvo ne obrati, doći će kazna gora od potopa, a stradat će i nedužni, mnogi svećenici i dobri vjernici. To su, zaključuje, duhovni zakoni. Zato su vjernici dužni opominjati sugrađane da se ne poigravaju s Bogom jer je krajnje vrijeme za obraćenje. Dio završava molitvom: „Bože, spasi nas od onoga što dolazi.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak opravdano poziva na obraćenje i prepoznaje da većina ne može glasovanjem učiniti moralno zlo dobrim; demokracija je politički oblik, a ne vrhovno mjerilo istine. Ipak, govor o tome da Bog „obrezuje narod” i prepušta ga đavlu kao objašnjenje nacionalnih nesreća iznosi se previše kategorično, bez dovoljne razlike između Božje pravednosti, dopuštanja zla i patnje nevinih.
concerns: Iz opće biblijske teme narodnog grijeha ne slijedi da se određena politička odluka ili nesreća može pouzdano protumačiti kao Božja kazna. Crkveni tekst izričito upozorava da nesreća ne objašnjava uvijek osobni grijeh te spominje i patnju nevinih.

Tvrdnja da narod koji se klanja idolu time prepušta vlast đavlu može biti duhovna metafora, ali bez pojašnjenja zvuči kao neposredan i siguran uzrok političkih događaja. Kritika pretjeranog nacionalizma opravdana je kad se nacija postavlja iznad Boga i moralnog zakona, no odlomak ne razlikuje takvo idolopoklonstvo od legitimne ljubavi prema domovini.

Poruku iz Akite i najavu kazne „gore od potopa” ne treba predstavljati kao sigurnu, obvezujuću prognozu. Dostupni izvori ne potvrđuju tu konkretnu tvrdnju; poziv na obraćenje može se prihvatiti bez zaključka da se najavljena kazna sigurno mora dogoditi.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički govor o Božjoj kazni treba povezati s Božjom pravednošću i milosrđem: nevolja može biti poziv na obraćenje, ali nije dopušteno automatski zaključiti da je žrtva ili pogođeni narod kažnjen zbog određenog grijeha. Demokratska odluka ne određuje sama po sebi što je moralno dobro, ali ni samo postojanje demokracije nije protivno vjeri; presudno je poštuje li politički život istinu, dostojanstvo osobe i moralni zakon.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage justifiedly calls for conversion and recognizes that the majority cannot through voting make a moral evil good; democracy is a political form, rather than the supreme measure of truth. Nevertheless, speaking of God "circumcising the nation" and abandoning it to the devil as an explanation for national disasters is presented too categorically, without sufficient distinction between God's justice, the permission of evil, and the suffering of the innocent.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic discourse on divine punishment should be connected with God's justice and mercy: affliction can be a call to conversion, but it is not permissible to conclude automatically that a victim or affected nation is punished because of a specific sin. A democratic decision does not in itself determine what is morally good, but the mere existence of democracy is not contrary to faith either; what is decisive is whether political life respects truth, human dignity, and the moral law.
concerns_en: From the general biblical theme of national sin, it does not follow that a specific political decision or misfortune can be reliably interpreted as divine punishment. Church texts explicitly warn that misfortune does not always explain personal sin and also mention the suffering of the innocent.

The claim that a people who worship an idol thereby cede authority to the devil can be a spiritual metaphor, but without clarification sounds like an immediate and certain cause of political events. Criticism of excessive nationalism is justified when the nation is placed above God and the moral law, but the passage does not distinguish such idolatry from legitimate love for the homeland.

The message from Akita and the announcement of punishment "worse than the Deluge" should not be presented as a certain, binding forecast. Available sources do not confirm that specific claim; the call to conversion can be accepted without concluding that the announced punishment must certainly happen.

sections.subtitle_en: When a nation goes astray: Ireland, democracy, and the warning from Akita
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar cites Irish referendums as an example of a nation going astray
sections.content_en:
“A nation can fall ill”, warns Grebenar, and asserts that **democracy is not a fundamental value the way God sees it**. As an example, he mentions **Ireland**: the Irish people voted in two referendums first for the right to abortion, and then for the right of same-sex couples to adopt children. He recalls that twenty years ago Catholics took pride in "Catholic Ireland", yet it, he says, enacted "Satan's laws" on its own.

Sacred Scripture, especially the Old Testament, teaches that an entire nation or the greater part of it can take the wrong direction. When the majority scorns what is God's, God allows something painful in order to **circumcise the nation**. He draws a comparison with the individual: whoever does not humble themselves before God through fasting and does not crucify their own flesh, God will humble in His own way in order to mend them.

If a nation bows down to the devil and chooses him instead of the heavenly Father, God, in Grebenar's interpretation, justly allows it: the one whom the nation worships begins to rule over it. Among such idols he also includes **nationalism**, excessive love toward the flag, Croathood, Serbhood, or Americanism, as in Germany during Hitler's time. The devil, he says, does not know how to rule, only how to strike. Then the innocent also suffer and innocent blood is shed.

He recalls the message from **Akita**: if humanity does not convert, a chastisement worse than the deluge will come, and the innocent, many priests, and good faithful will also perish. Those are, he concludes, spiritual laws. Therefore, the faithful have a duty to admonish their fellow citizens not to play games with God because it is the eleventh hour for conversion. The segment ends with a prayer: "God, save us from what is coming."

sections.subtitle: Nakon posta: odmor s Isusom, a ne od Isusa
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava kako ustrajati nakon završetka 40-dnevnog posta
sections.content:
Nakon psalma „Spomeni se, Gospodine, svoje ljubavi“ Grebenar čita odlomak iz **Poslanice Rimljanima**. Svi koje vodi Duh Božji sinovi su Božji. Primili su duha posinstva u kojem kliču „Aba, Oče“. Patnje sadašnjeg vremena ništa su prema budućoj slavi, a **sve stvorenje uzdiše i muči se u porođajnim bolima** do sada.

Tumači da riječi svetog Pavla o „svem stvorenju“ znače da uzdiše svaki pojedinac. Primjenjuje ih na upravo završeni četrdesetodnevni post. Oni koji su postili osjećaju se dobro, „lagani kao ptice“, mnogi su obiteljski problemi riješeni, mirniji su i Isus im je bliži. Ali neka ne poste deset ili petnaest dana, upozorava, pa će vidjeti kako se sve vraća.

Vjernik ne može ne postiti, ne ići na misu i ne moliti. Svaki je dan, kaže, utakmica i bitka za spasenje. Dopušta da se treba znati zaustaviti i odmoriti od posta, ali **i odmor mora biti molitva**. Ne smije se Isusu reći: „Sad je završio post, ćao, idem svojim putem na petnaest dana odmora od tebe.“ Tko tako govori, kaže, već je zgriješio i đavao dolazi odmah.

Nudi i ispravnu molitvu: „Isuse, završila sam s postom. Sad me ti odmori, pripremi me za nove zadaće, daj mi milost da uživam u tvojoj prisutnosti.“ Od Isusa se, poručuje, nije moguće i nije dopušteno odvojiti. Uzdišu i obitelji, jer danas nije jednostavno odgajati djecu, a uzdišu i narod i cijela Crkva.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak dobro naglašava ustrajnost u molitvi i životu s Kristom te prikladno prikazuje post kao duhovno sredstvo, a ne cilj sam po sebi. No poistovjetiti „sve stvorenje” s uzdahom svakého pojedinca ograničava Pavlovu širu sliku, a tvrdnja da je grijeh uzeti odmor od posta može opteretiti savjest jače nego što nauk opravdava.
concerns: U Rim 8,19–23 „sve stvorenje” nije jednostavno drugo ime za svakog pojedinca: Pavlova slika obuhvaća stvorenje koje čeka oslobođenje i povezuje ga s nadom vjernika. Osobna patnja i obiteljske teškoće mogu biti primjena teksta, ali ne iscrpljuju njegovo značenje.

Post je važna praksa, ali nije obveza svakog vjernika da neprekidno posti, niti je samo prestajanje s dobrovoljnim postom nakon četrdeset dana grijeh. Crkveni izvor izričito prikazuje i tjelesni odmor, ako se živi u Duhu, kao nešto što se može prinositi Bogu; drugi izvor opisuje post kao dio puta uz molitvu i ljubav, ne kao zamjenu za njih.

Rečenica da onaj tko se odmara od posta „već je zgriješio” spaja odmor od posta s prekidom odnosa s Isusom. Treba razlikovati napuštanje molitve i vjere od razboritog odmora ili povratka uobičajenoj prehrani.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao u Rim 8 govori i o sadašnjoj patnji i o budućoj slavi, pa „porođajne boli” upućuju na iščekivanje obnove, a ne samo na pojedinačni osjećaj umora ili probleme u obitelji. Kršćanski post ima smisla kad vodi molitvi, obraćenju i ljubavi; odmor ne mora značiti udaljavanje od Boga, jer i svakodnevni život i tjelesno opuštanje mogu postati duhovni prinos ako se žive u Duhu.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage rightly emphasizes perseverance in prayer and life with Christ and appropriately presents fasting as a spiritual means, rather than an end in itself. However, equating "all creation" with the sigh of each individual limits Paul's broader picture, and the claim that it is a sin to take a rest from fasting can burden conscience more heavily than doctrine justifies.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul in Rom 8 speaks both of present suffering and future glory, so "labor pains" point to the longing for renewal, and not merely to an individual feeling of tiredness or problems in the family. Christian fasting makes sense when it leads to prayer, conversion, and love; rest does not have to mean turning away from God, because everyday life and physical relaxation can also become a spiritual offering if lived in the Spirit.
concerns_en: In Rom 8:19–23 "all creation" is not simply another name for each individual: Paul's image encompasses creation awaiting liberation and connects it with the hope of believers. Personal suffering and family difficulties can be an application of the text, but do not exhaust its meaning.

Fasting is an important practice, but it is not an obligation of every believer to fast continuously, nor is simply ceasing voluntary fasting after forty days a sin. An ecclesial source explicitly presents physical rest as well, if lived in the Spirit, as something that can be offered to God; another source describes fasting as part of the path alongside prayer and love, not as a replacement for them.

The sentence that whoever rests from fasting "has already sinned" conflates rest from fasting with severing one's relationship with Jesus. One must distinguish abandoning prayer and faith from prudent rest or returning to a customary diet.

sections.subtitle_en: After the fast: rest with Jesus, not from Jesus
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host explains how to persevere after the end of the 40-day fast
sections.content_en:
After the psalm "Remember, Lord, Your love", Grebenar reads a passage from the **Epistle to the Romans**. All who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. They have received the spirit of adoption in which they cry out, "Abba, Father". The sufferings of the present time are nothing compared to the future glory, and **all creation has been groaning and travailing in labor pains** until now.

He interprets Saint Paul's words about "all creation" to mean that every individual groans. He applies them to the just-concluded forty-day fast. Those who fasted feel good, "light as birds", many family problems have been resolved, they are calmer, and Jesus is closer to them. But let them not fast for ten or fifteen days, he warns, and they will see how everything returns.

A believer cannot fail to fast, fail to go to Mass, and fail to pray. Every day, he says, is a match and a battle for salvation. He grants that one must know how to pause and take a rest from fasting, but **rest too must be prayer**. One must not say to Jesus: "Now the fast has ended, bye, I'm going my own way for fifteen days of rest from You." Whoever speaks like that, he says, has already sinned and the devil comes immediately.

He also offers the proper prayer: "Jesus, I have finished fasting. Now You rest me, prepare me for new tasks, give me the grace to enjoy Your presence." From Jesus, he conveys, it is not possible and not permissible to separate oneself. Families groan too, because today it is not easy to raise children, and both the nation and the whole Church groan.

sections.subtitle: Porođajna bol i majčinstvo kao slika pročišćenja
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar opisuje majčinsku žrtvu i besane noći uz bolesno dijete
sections.content:
„Nema spasenja, nema vječnosti bez prolaska kroz porođajne boli“, kaže Grebenar. Uz tjelesno obrezanje uvodi još jednu sliku bolnog obrezanja srca: **porođajnu bol**. Žene znaju koliko porođaj boli, a ta bol je, tumači, slika ljudskog pročišćenja.

Trpljenje porođaja ženu priprema da se može predati djetetu. Nakon toga dolazi nova bol, koju u ljubavi podnosi za dijete. Opisuje je vrlo konkretno: dijete se budi noću, treba ga dojiti, dobije temperaturu, majka bdije noć i dan, pa se dogodi da u pet dana ukupno odspava deset sati. Tko ima djecu, kaže, zna što je to, a tko nema, teško može razumjeti. Još je teže kad istekne porodiljni dopust pa treba ići na posao, a dijete je bolesno i nema ga se kome ostaviti. Ako ide u vrtić, može se očekivati da će ondje opet dobiti temperaturu, i tako u krug.

Kako se ipak ide naprijed? **Kršćani se ne boje**, kaže Grebenar, nego idu u susret problemu i izazovu i gledaju naprijed. Tko gleda samo koliko će biti teško roditi i odgojiti dijete, taj neće dijete jer više voli sebe. Navodi i oca koji kaže „dosta je jedno, i jedno je previše“. Takve roditelje, smatra, ne vodi obrezano srce. Obrezanje srca znači predanje: **više ne živiš sebi, nego za drugoga**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak dobro ističe da roditeljska ljubav može uključivati predanje, žrtvu i podnošenje teškoća, ali tvrdnja da nema spasenja ni vječnosti bez „porođajnih boli“ teološki je preširoka i može zvučati kao da je sama bol nužan uvjet spasenja. Također neopravdano zaključuje da roditelji koji žele jedno dijete ili razmatraju teškoće roditeljstva imaju neobrezano srce, premda Crkva priznaje odgovorno i razborito odlučivanje o broju djece.
concerns: Izraz „nema spasenja, nema vječnosti bez prolaska kroz porođajne boli“ može poistovjetiti spasenje s tjelesnom boli ili jednim posebnim oblikom roditeljskog iskustva. Pio XII. navodi da majčinstvo donosi mnogo toga što majka mora podnijeti, ali i da Sveto pismo ne određuje točan način na koji se to ostvaruje; taj izvor ne opravdava tvrdnju da je porođajna bol univerzalni uvjet spasenja.

Povezivanje odluke „dosta je jedno“ s manjkom obrezanja srca ne uzima dovoljno u obzir odgovorno roditeljstvo: katolički nauk dopušta supružnicima da iz ozbiljnih razloga i uz poštovanje moralnog zakona odluče ne imati dodatnu djecu kroz određeno ili neodređeno vrijeme. Odluka ne smije proizlaziti iz sebičnosti niti nijekati vrijednost roditeljstva, ali sam broj djece ne dokazuje sebičan motiv.

Snažan govor o žrtvi može ostaviti dojam da je majčinska patnja sama po sebi ideal ili da se njezino ublažavanje ne uklapa u kršćansko predanje. Pio XII. izričito kaže da Sveto pismo ne zabranjuje sredstva koja olakšavaju porod te da je pružanje djelotvorne psihičke i fizičke pomoći majkama izraz kršćanske ljubavi.
magisterium.enrichment: Porođajna bol može poslužiti kao slika truda i žrtvene ljubavi, ali takva slika ne treba se pretvoriti u pravilo da je bol potrebna za spasenje ili mjerilo svetosti roditelja. U katoličkom razumijevanju odgovorno roditeljstvo uključuje i velikodušnu otvorenost životu i razboritu brigu za djecu koju roditelji već imaju, njihove mogućnosti odgoja te konkretne okolnosti.
