citations.document_title: Address on moral and religious dictates concerning natural painless childbirth (8 January 1956)

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage rightly emphasizes that parental love can include surrender, sacrifice, and enduring difficulties, but the claim that there is no salvation or eternity without "labor pains" is theologically too broad and can sound as though pain itself is a necessary condition of salvation. It also unjustifiably concludes that parents who want one child or consider the difficulties of parenthood have an uncircumcised heart, even though the Church recognizes responsible and prudent decision-making regarding family size.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Labor pain can serve as an image of effort and sacrificial love, but such an image should not be turned into a rule that pain is necessary for salvation or a measure of parents' holiness. In the Catholic understanding, responsible parenthood includes both a generous openness to life and prudent care for the children parents already have, their possibilities for education, and concrete circumstances.
concerns_en: The expression "there is no salvation, there is no eternity without passing through labor pains" can equate salvation with physical pain or one particular form of parental experience. Pius XII states that motherhood brings much that a mother must endure, but also that Sacred Scripture does not determine the exact manner in which this is realized; that source does not justify the claim that labor pain is a universal condition of salvation.

Connecting the decision "one is enough" with a lack of circumcision of the heart does not take responsible parenthood sufficiently into account: Catholic teaching permits spouses for serious reasons and with respect for the moral law to decide not to have additional children for a certain or indefinite period. The decision must not arise from selfishness nor deny the value of parenthood, but the number of children alone does not prove a selfish motive.

Strong language about sacrifice can leave the impression that maternal suffering is an ideal in itself or that its alleviation does not fit with Christian dedication. Pius XII explicitly says that Sacred Scripture does not forbid means that facilitate childbirth and that providing effective psychological and physical assistance to mothers is an expression of Christian charity.

sections.subtitle_en: Labor pain and motherhood as an image of purification
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar describes maternal sacrifice and sleepless nights with a sick child
sections.content_en:
“There is no salvation, there is no eternity without passing through labor pains”, says Grebenar. Alongside physical circumcision, he introduces another image of painful circumcision of the heart: **labor pain**. Women know how much childbirth hurts, and that pain is, he interprets, an image of human purification.

The suffering of childbirth prepares a woman to be able to surrender herself to the child. After that comes a new pain, which she bears in love for the child. He describes it very concretely: the child wakes at night, needs breastfeeding, gets a fever, the mother keeps vigil night and day, so it happens that in five days she sleeps a total of ten hours. Whoever has children, he says, knows what that is, and whoever does not can hardly understand. It is even harder when maternity leave expires and one must go to work, while the child is sick and there is no one to leave it with. If the child goes to kindergarten, it can be expected that it will get a fever there again, and so in a loop.

How does one nevertheless move forward? **Christians are not afraid**, says Grebenar, but go out to meet the problem and challenge and look forward. Whoever looks only at how difficult it will be to give birth and raise a child does not want a child because they love themselves more. He also mentions a father who says "one is enough, and one is too much". Such parents, he considers, are not led by a circumcised heart. Circumcision of the heart means surrender: **you no longer live for yourself, but for another**.

sections.subtitle: Svjedočanstvo: odricanje od košarke radi obitelji
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar svjedoči kako je u 26. godini prekinuo s košarkom
sections.content:
Da se mnogočega treba odreći, Grebenar potkrepljuje vlastitim iskustvom. Igrao je **profesionalnu košarku** i trenirao dvaput dnevno. Kasnije je prešao u drugu ligu, „poluprofesionalno, poluamaterski“, s jednim treningom dnevno. Kada mu se rodilo prvo dijete, sve se promijenilo.

Shvatio je da mu je košarka postala konkurencija vremenu s djetetom i pomoći u obitelji, gdje je najveći teret nosila supruga. Zato je **s 26 godina prestao igrati**. Odlučio je da je za obitelj korisnije to vrijeme uložiti u nastavak školovanja. Potom su došli drugo i treće dijete. Otprilike pet godina nije išao ni na košarku ni na nogomet, iako ih silno voli i s loptom je od djetinjstva, „u krvi, u nogama i u srcu“. Djecu su supruga i on podizali sami, oboje su radili, a kod kuće su ga čekali djeca i supruga.

Sjeća se koliko je bio sretan kada je nakon pet godina prvi put opet zaigrao nogomet. Kaže da mu nije bilo žao i da se tim iskustvom, ako smije reći, ponosi. Zahvaljuje Bogu što ga je kroz tih pet godina **očistio od navezanosti** i dao mu nešto važnije. Poslije mu je igra bila još draža: mogao je igrati i zabaviti se, ali nije morao i ništa mu nije nedostajalo. Završava riječima svetog Pavla: „Sve mogu u onome koji me jača.“

magisterium.assessment: Osobno svjedočanstvo prikazuje vjerodostojan oblik samoodricanja: odricanje od nečega voljenog, kada se razborito vidi da to konkurira vremenu i pomoći potrebnima obitelji. Ono je uglavnom usklađeno s katoličkim naukom, uz važnu ogradu da takva osobna odluka nije univerzalna obveza za sve roditelje niti dokaz da je bavljenje sportom samo po sebi sebično.
concerns: Iskustvo može zvučati kao opće mjerilo prema kojem roditelj mora odustati od sporta ili druge osobne aktivnosti. Odluka koju je Grebenar donio može biti primjer velikodušnog razlučivanja, ali iz odlomka ne slijedi da je to jedini ispravan izbor za svaku obitelj.

Citat „Sve mogu u onome koji me jača“ ispravno upućuje na snagu u Kristu, ali ne znači da će kršćanin moći postići bilo koji željeni ishod ili da će mu biti uklonjene sve teškoće. Pavlove riječi naglašavaju oslanjanje na Krista usred životnih okolnosti i kušnji.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni dokument o sportu prepoznaje da sport može odgajati samodisciplinu, poniznost, ustrajnost i jakost te da odricanje ima smisla kada je usmjereno ljubavi. Zato svjedočanstvo ne treba tumačiti kao osudu košarke ili nogometa, nego kao primjer razboritog prepoznavanja prioriteta u određenom razdoblju života. Pavlovu završnu rečenicu najbolje je razumjeti kao pouzdanje u Krista koji daje snagu za vjernost pozivu i u teškoćama, a ne kao obećanje neograničenog uspjeha.

citations.document_title: Giving the best of yourself. A document on the Christian perspective on sport and the human person (1 June 2018)
citations.document_author: Dicastery for Laity, Family and Life

magisterium.assessment_en: The personal testimony presents a credible form of self-denial: giving up something loved, when it is prudently seen that it competes with the time and assistance needed by the family. It is largely aligned with Catholic teaching, with the important qualification that such a personal decision is not a universal obligation for all parents nor proof that engaging in sports is selfish in itself.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church document on sports recognizes that sport can foster self-discipline, humility, perseverance, and fortitude, and that renunciation makes sense when directed toward love. Therefore, the testimony should not be interpreted as a condemnation of basketball or soccer, but as an example of prudent recognition of priorities in a particular period of life. Paul's concluding sentence is best understood as trust in Christ who gives strength for fidelity to one's calling also in difficulties, rather than as a promise of unlimited success.
concerns_en: The experience can sound like a general standard according to which a parent must give up sports or another personal activity. The decision that Grebenar made can be an example of generous discernment, but from the passage it does not follow that it is the only correct choice for every family.

The quotation "I can do all things in him who strengthens me" correctly points to strength in Christ, but does not mean that a Christian will be able to achieve any desired outcome or that all difficulties will be removed. Paul's words emphasize reliance on Christ in the midst of life's circumstances and trials.

sections.subtitle_en: Testimony: giving up basketball for the sake of the family
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar testifies how at age 26 he stopped playing basketball
sections.content_en:
That many things must be renounced Grebenar substantiates with his own experience. He played **professional basketball** and trained twice a day. Later he moved to the second league, "semi-professionally, semi-amateurly", with one training session a day. When his first child was born, everything changed.

He realized that basketball had become competition for time with the child and helping out in the family, where his wife bore the greatest burden. Therefore, **at age 26 he stopped playing**. He decided it was more beneficial for the family to invest that time in continuing his education. Then came the second and third children. For about five years he did not play basketball or soccer, although he loves them immensely and has been with a ball since childhood, "in the blood, in the legs, and in the heart". His wife and he raised the children by themselves, both worked, and at home his children and wife awaited him.

He remembers how happy he was when, after five years, he played soccer again for the first time. He says he did not regret it and that he is proud of that experience, if he may say so. He thanks God that over those five years He **cleansed him of attachment** and gave him something more important. Later, playing was even sweeter to him: he could play and have fun, but he did not have to, and he lacked nothing. He concludes with the words of Saint Paul: "I can do all things through Him who strengthens me."

sections.subtitle: Između progresivaca i nacionalista: Crkva kao treći put
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači Gospinu poruku od 25. listopada
sections.content:
Iz osobnih navezanosti Grebenar prelazi na **navezanosti naroda** i upozorava da se ne griješi ni osobnim grijesima ni grijesima naroda. Narodi svijeta danas su, kaže, podijeljeni u **dva tabora**.

Prvi je ljevičarski, liberalan i „progresivan“, ali njegov progres vodi, tvrdi, „prema dolje, u smrt, u pakao“, a ne prema nebu i slobodi. U Hrvatskoj su to po njegovim riječima oni koji se predstavljaju kao antifašisti. Drugi tabor je **nacionalizam**, zaljubljenost u vlastitu naciju, koji također vodi u pakao. Oba tabora danas istodobno rastu i, prema Grebenaru, dolaze od istog duha, **duha antikrista**.

Kao odgovor ističe rast **Crkve**, „nešto treće“ što Bog daje. Poziva se na Gospinu poruku od **25. listopada** i kaže da je treba dobro pročitati. Mržnja i rat šire se ljudskim srcima jer ljudi gledaju svoje sebične interese, a Bog im želi dati mir koji oni ne žele. Grebenar dodaje da mnogi koji idu u crkvu i nazivaju se Hrvatima i katolicima ne žele mir, jer **duh nacionalizma, kad jača, priprema narod za rat**.

Zato poziva hrvatske katolike da se ne ujedinjuju na ideji hrvatstva, nego **oko križa**. Križ, ističe, nije ideja nego poziv. Ako križ nije na prvom mjestu i u središtu ujedinjenja, „neće biti dobro“. Progresivci križ preziru, a nacionalisti ga koriste kao sredstvo za ostvarenje nacionalnih interesa i rješavanje „hrvatskog pitanja“. To pitanje i podjele u društvu može riješiti samo Krist Gospodin, ali tek ako ga ljudi stave na prvo mjesto, jer je za njih umro na križu.

magisterium.assessment: Središnji poziv da se nacija ne pretvara u apsolut i da se mir i zajedništvo temelje na Kristu u skladu je s katoličkim naukom: Pio XI. upozorava na neurednu ljubav prema domovini koja vlastiti narod čini idolom, a Crkva je pozvana na univerzalnu ljubav i mir. Ipak, tvrdnje da dva politička tabora potječu od istoga „duha antikrista” te da nacionalizam nužno priprema narod za rat preširoke su ako se odnose na čitave skupine, a ne na konkretne ideje i postupke.
concerns: Prikaz ljevice/progresivaca i nacionalista kao dvaju jedinstvenih tabora koji nužno vode u propast pojednostavljuje raznolike političke stavove i ne razlikuje pogrešne ideologije od osoba koje ih zastupaju.

Katolički nauk upozorava na pretjerani nacionalizam, ali ne poistovjećuje svaku ljubav prema domovini ili nacionalni identitet s grijehom; domoljublje ne mora uključivati prezir prema drugim narodima.
Pozivanje na Gospinu poruku ne može samo po sebi potvrditi političku prosudbu; poruke privatnih objava treba razlučivati u skladu s vjerom i moralom Crkve.
magisterium.enrichment: Pio XI. povezuje molitvu za mir s odbacivanjem težnje za dominacijom i neuredne ljubavi prema vlastitom narodu, a Krista naziva „našim mirom” (Ef 2,14). Kršćanski je cilj zato domoljublje pročišćeno ljubavlju prema svim narodima, a ne uklanjanje legitimne brige za vlastiti narod. Kritika treba biti usmjerena na idolopoklonstvo, mržnju i nepravdu, bez olakog pripisivanja zlih pobuda cijelim političkim skupinama.
magisterium.assessment_en: The central call not to turn the nation into an absolute and that peace and unity be based on Christ is in accordance with Catholic teaching: Pius XI warns against disordered love for the homeland that makes one's own people an idol, and the Church is called to universal love and peace. Nevertheless, claims that two political camps originate from the same "spirit of the Antichrist" and that nationalism necessarily prepares a people for war are too broad if applied to entire groups, rather than to concrete ideas and actions.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Pius XI connects prayer for peace with the rejection of the desire for domination and disordered love for one's own people, and calls Christ "our peace" (Eph 2:14). The Christian goal is therefore patriotism purified by love for all nations, rather than the elimination of legitimate care for one's own people. Criticism should be directed at idolatry, hatred, and injustice, without lightly attributing evil motives to entire political groups.
concerns_en: Presenting the left/progressives and nationalists as two unified camps that necessarily lead to ruin simplifies diverse political positions and fails to distinguish erroneous ideologies from the persons who advocate them.
Catholic teaching warns against excessive nationalism, but does not equate every love for the homeland or national identity with sin; patriotism does not have to include contempt for other nations.
Invoking Our Lady's message cannot in itself confirm a political judgment; messages of private revelations must be discerned in accordance with the faith and morals of the Church.

sections.subtitle_en: Between progressives and nationalists: the Church as a third path
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host interprets Our Lady's message of October 25
sections.content_en:
From personal attachments, Grebenar moves to the **attachments of nations** and warns against sinning either through personal sins or the sins of a nation. The nations of the world today are, he says, divided into **two camps**.

The first is leftist, liberal, and "progressive", but its progress leads, he asserts, "downward, into death, into hell", and not toward heaven and freedom. In Croatia, according to his words, these are those who present themselves as anti-fascists. The second camp is **nationalism**, falling in love with one's own nation, which likewise leads to hell. Both camps are growing simultaneously today and, according to Grebenar, come from the same spirit, the **spirit of the antichrist**.

As a response, he points to the growth of the **Church**, "something third" that God provides. He refers to Our Lady's message of **October 25** and says it must be read carefully. Hatred and war are spreading through human hearts because people look to their selfish interests, while God wants to give them peace that they do not want. Grebenar adds that many who go to church and call themselves Croats and Catholics do not want peace, because **the spirit of nationalism, as it grows stronger, prepares a nation for war**.

He therefore calls on Croatian Catholics not to unite on the idea of Croathood, but **around the cross**. The cross, he emphasizes, is not an idea but a calling. If the cross is not in the first place and at the center of unification, "it will not be good". Progressives despise the cross, while nationalists use it as a tool to achieve national interests and resolve the "Croatian question". That question and the divisions in society can be resolved only by Christ the Lord, but only if people put Him first, because He died on the cross for them.

sections.subtitle: Kritika ujedinjenja desnice bez Krista
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar upozorava na opasnost ujedinjenja desnice koje nije utemeljeno na Kristu
sections.content:
Grebenar izravno kritizira dio hrvatske političke scene. Problem je, kaže, kada pojedine **desne političke stranke ne vjeruju u Isusa svim srcem**, nego u svoje fotelje i utjecaj, na drugoj strani vide neprijatelje, a križ i Crkva im služe za vlastite ideje. To, upozorava, vodi u propast cijelog naroda i tu opasnost treba spriječiti.

Odbacuje svako ujedinjenje desnice koje se ne temelji na križu, Svetom pismu i Božjoj riječi, nego samo na rušenju komunizma i antifašizma. Takvo **„ujedinjenje desnice“, kaže, zapravo i ne postoji**. Umjesto toga treba rasti zajednica onih koji su Kristovi, u hrvatskom narodu i u narodima svijeta. To su ljudi koji vjeruju u Isusa, mole i poste, ali čine i nešto više od toga.

Kada križ bude temeljna vrijednost, Bog će, poručuje, učiniti sve za što vjernici mole, ukloniti nepravdu te razoriti sotonska djela i lažne utvrde u Hrvatskoj, kako on kaže, antifašizma i komunizma.

magisterium.assessment: Opravdano je upozorenje da se križ i Crkva ne smiju instrumentalizirati za stranačke interese te da se političko djelovanje mora prosuđivati prema Kristu i moralnom zakonu. Međutim, poistovjećivanje antifašizma kao takvog s „djelima sotone” te tvrdnja da će Bog učiniti sve što se moli ako križ bude politički temelj iznose neopravdano opće zaključke i mogu stvarati dojam da molitva jamči određene političke ishode.
concerns: Kritika političkog korištenja križa opravdana je, ali tekst ne razlikuje dovoljno između instrumentalizacije vjere i legitimnog političkog zalaganja nadahnutog kršćanskim načelima.

Antifašizam nije sam po sebi isto što i komunizam niti se na temelju priloženih izvora može proglasiti sotonskim djelom; Pio XII. osuđuje idoliziranje rase, naroda ili države, ali to ne opravdava takvu opću osudu antifašizma.
Formulacija da će Bog učiniti „sve za što vjernici mole” može sugerirati automatsko ispunjenje molitvenih zahtjeva ili politički uspjeh, umjesto pouzdanja u Boga uz prihvaćanje njegove volje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko protivljenje bezbožnom komunizmu ne uklanja potrebu da se političke tvrdnje i sredstva prosuđuju pojedinačno; osuda komunizma ne czyni svaku suprotnu ideologiju ili politički pokret automatski kršćanskim. Pio XI. također uči da mir među ljudima traži unutarnju pravednost i ljubav, pa molitva i post ne zamjenjuju odgovornost za pravedno djelovanje. Kršćansko političko zajedništvo može biti nadahnuto vjerom, ali ne smije svesti Krista na jamstvo programa, stranke ili nacionalnog cilja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The warning that the cross and the Church must not be instrumentalized for partisan interests and that political action must be judged according to Christ and the moral law is justified. However, equating anti-fascism as such with "the works of Satan" and claiming that God will do everything that is prayed for if the cross is the political foundation make unjustified general conclusions and can create the impression that prayer guarantees certain political outcomes.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic opposition to godless communism does not remove the need for political claims and means to be judged individually; condemnation of communism does not make every contrary ideology or political movement automatically Christian. Pius XI also teaches that peace among men requires inner justice and love, so prayer and fasting do not replace the responsibility for just action. Christian political unity can be inspired by faith, but must not reduce Christ to a guarantee of a program, party, or national goal.
concerns_en: Criticism of the political use of the cross is justified, but the text does not sufficiently distinguish between the instrumentalization of faith and legitimate political engagement inspired by Christian principles.

Anti-fascism is not in itself the same as communism, nor can it on the basis of the attached sources be declared a satanic work; Pius XII condemns the idolization of race, nation, or state, but that does not justify such a general condemnation of anti-fascism.

The formulation that God will do "everything the faithful pray for" can suggest an automatic fulfillment of prayer requests or political success, instead of trust in God alongside acceptance of his will.

sections.subtitle_en: Criticism of unifying the right without Christ
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar warns of the danger of unifying the right that is not founded on Christ
sections.content_en:
Grebenar directly criticizes part of the Croatian political scene. The problem is, he says, when individual **right-wing political parties do not believe in Jesus with all their heart**, but in their armchairs and influence, see enemies on the other side, and the cross and the Church serve them for their own ideas. That, he warns, leads to the ruin of the entire nation, and that danger must be prevented.

He rejects any unification of the right that is not based on the cross, Sacred Scripture, and the Word of God, but merely on the tearing down of communism and anti-fascism. Such **“unification of the right”, he says, does not actually exist**. Instead, the community of those who belong to Christ must grow, within the Croatian nation and among the nations of the world. These are people who believe in Jesus, pray, and fast, but also do something more than that.

When the cross becomes the fundamental value, God will, he conveys, do everything the faithful pray for, remove injustice, and tear down Satan's works and false strongholds in Croatia, as he says, of anti-fascism and communism.

sections.subtitle: Plodovi posta: zgrada Vjesnika i kosti žrtava iz Slovenije
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj povezuje post s povratkom posmrtnih ostataka žrtava iz 1945.
sections.content:
Kao konkretne plodove Grebenar navodi događaje koje povezuje s postom. Zajednica je **40 dana postila i molila** da se razotkriju laži „komunističkih medija“ o žrtvama Drugog svjetskog rata, a nakon toga je, kaže, izgorjela zgrada **Vjesnika**. Takve se bitke, ističe, vode Božjom riječju, a ne političkim idejama, jer je riječ o duhovnom pokrivaču o kojem govori prorok Izaija.

Drugi primjer je **povratak kostiju iz Slovenije**, posmrtnih ostataka hrvatskih vojnika i civila ubijenih u svibnju 1945. godine. Prema njegovim riječima, to se dogodilo nakon 85 godina i tek kada su tisuće ljudi postile na tu nakanu. Hrvatski nadbiskup ih je pokopao katoličkim obredom, dostojanstveno. Grebenar pita koliki je prekrivač smrti nad Hrvatskom i Slovenijom kada desetljećima nije bilo moguće vratiti kosti ubijenih i dostojno ih pokopati.

Prenosi i riječi jednog bivšeg hrvatskog ministra zdravstva: kad god bi se nešto pokušalo, čak i uz pristanak ljevice, uvijek bi se nešto ispriječilo, što je ministar nazvao nevjerojatnim. Grebenar to tumači kao djelovanje **duhova smrti**, velikog tamnog oblaka koji priječi. Kada se ciljano posti i moli protiv toga, Bog, kaže, razara te utvrde.

Zgradu Vjesnika opisuje kao zgradu koju je osnovala Komunistička partija Hrvatske „da piše laži i sakrije istinu“. U njoj su, tvrdi, bila dva kata Udbe koja su nadzirala informacije koje izlaze van. „To su Božji ratovi, to su Božje bitke“, zaključuje.

magisterium.assessment: Post i molitva legitimni su oblici kršćanske duhovne borbe, a dostojanstven pokop žrtava poštuje ljudsko dostojanstvo. Ipak, prikazivanje požara i dugogodišnjih političkih prepreka kao dokazanih plodova posta ili djelovanja duhova smrti iznosi nedokazane uzročne i duhovne zaključke.
concerns: Vremenski slijed događaja nakon posta ne dokazuje da ih je post prouzročio niti da je požar bio Božji odgovor; takvo tumačenje može religiozno opravdati spekulaciju.

Pripisivanje političkih i povijesnih prepreka duhovima smrti bez razboritog ispitivanja činjenica pretjerano je sigurno. Crkva traži kritičku procjenu mogućih demonskih djelovanja, oprez i razlučivanje te upozorava da se zlo ne koristi kao prelagano objašnjenje događaja.
Tvrdnje o osnutku Vjesnika, ulozi Udbe i političkom prikrivanju povijesti u prikazanom odlomku iznesene su kao činjenice, ali dostupni izvori ne omogućuju njihovu provjeru.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva potvrđuje vrijednost posta i molitve, ali oni nisu mehanizam kojim se može zajamčiti određeni politički ili povijesni ishod; kršćanska molitva uzdaje se u Boga, a ne zaključuje automatski o njegovoj namjeri iz vremenskog slijeda događaja. U pogledu duhovnog zla, vjera ne isključuje njegovo djelovanje, ali zahtijeva trezvenost i razlučivanje, uz očuvanje ljudske odgovornosti i slobode.

magisterium.assessment_en: Fasting and prayer are legitimate forms of Christian spiritual warfare, and the dignified burial of victims respects human dignity. Nevertheless, presenting fires and longstanding political obstacles as proven fruits of fasting or the action of spirits of death makes unproven causal and spiritual conclusions.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church confirms the value of fasting and prayer, but they are not a mechanism by which a particular political or historical outcome can be guaranteed; Christian prayer trusts in God, and does not automatically conclude about his intent from the temporal sequence of events. With regard to spiritual evil, faith does not exclude its action, but requires sobriety and discernment, while preserving human responsibility and freedom.
concerns_en: The temporal sequence of events after the fast does not prove that the fast caused them nor that the fire was God's response; such an interpretation can religiously justify speculation.

Attributing political and historical obstacles to spirits of death without a prudent examination of the facts is overly confident. The Church requires critical assessment of possible demonic actions, caution, and discernment, and warns against using evil as an overly easy explanation of events.
Claims about the founding of Vjesnik, the role of Udba, and the political concealment of history in the presented passage are stated as facts, but available sources do not permit their verification.

sections.subtitle_en: Fruits of fasting: the Vjesnik building and bones of victims from Slovenia
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host connects fasting with the return of mortal remains of victims from 1945
sections.content_en:
As concrete fruits, Grebenar cites events that he connects with fasting. The community **fasted and prayed for 40 days** that the lies of the "communist media" about the victims of World War II be exposed, and after that, he says, the **Vjesnik** building burned down. Such battles, he points out, are fought with God's word and not with political ideas, because it is a matter of the spiritual veil spoken of by the prophet Isaiah.

The second example is the **return of bones from Slovenia**, the mortal remains of Croatian soldiers and civilians killed in May 1945. According to his words, that happened after 85 years and only when thousands of people fasted for that intention. A Croatian archbishop buried them with a Catholic rite, with dignity. Grebenar asks how great the covering of death over Croatia and Slovenia must be when for decades it was impossible to return the bones of the slain and bury them with dignity.

He also conveys the words of a former Croatian minister of health: whenever something was attempted, even with the consent of the left, something would always stand in the way, which the minister called unbelievable. Grebenar interprets this as the working of **spirits of death**, a great dark cloud that obstructs. When targeted fasting and prayer are made against it, God, he says, destroys those strongholds.

He describes the Vjesnik building as a building founded by the Communist Party of Croatia "to write lies and hide the truth". In it, he claims, were two floors of Udba that controlled the information going out. "These are God's wars, these are God's battles", he concludes.

sections.subtitle: Klin se klinom izbija: ustrajnost i kritika međureligijskih skupova
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar kritizira međureligijske susrete za mir
sections.content:
Unatoč tim plodovima, zlo je i dalje snažno prisutno, upozorava Grebenar, pa zajednica „nema drugog izbora“. **Klin se klinom izbija**: treba ostati zajedno u molitvi i postu. Izražava čvrsto uvjerenje da će Gospodin i nakon što ovaj podcast jednom završi održati na okupu zajednicu ljudi okupljenih oko molitve i posta, uvijek u jedinstvu sa „svetom majkom Crkvom“.

Na kraju se kratko osvrće na takozvani **„duh Asiza“**, međureligijske susrete na kojima predstavnici različitih religija, među njima i kršćani, zajedno govore o miru. Grebenar to naziva „igrokazom“ i smatra da od toga nema ništa. Opisuje to kao krivovjerje i „dijalog sa suvremenim svijetom“ koji **razara Crkvu iznutra**. Takvi skupovi, kaže, vjernicima poručuju da sve religije govore o dobru i da su sve od Boga. Tko tako postupa, tvrdi, nije branio Krista Gospodina i obezvrijedio je žrtvu na križu.

Naglašava da samo kršćani imaju Spasitelja, ali taj Spasitelj nije umro samo za njih, nego za cijeli svijet. Zato vjernici trebaju muslimanima, hinduistima, budistima i ateistima reći: **„Isus Krist umro je i za tebe.“**

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na ustrajnu molitvu i post te tvrdnja da je Isus umro za cijeli svijet sukladni su katoličkoj vjeri. Međutim, osuda duha Asiza kao krivovjerja i međureligijskih susreta kao razaranja Crkve ozbiljno je neusklađena s katoličkim naukom i tumačenjem koje je iznio Ivan Pavao II.
concerns: Ivan Pavao II. izričito je objasnio da susret u Asizu nije bio sinkretizam: sudionici su molili za mir ne odričući se svojih različitih vjerskih uvjerenja. Zato ga nazivati krivovjerjem peljudi koji su sudjelovali ili tvrdnjom da takvi susreti nužno razaraju Crkvu pogrešno predstavlja njegovu narav.

Katolički nauk istodobno potvrđuje da je spasenje samo u Kristu i da Crkva mora naviještati Krista te priznaje kako u drugim religijama mogu postojati elementi istine i dobrote. Poštovanje i dijalog ne znače da su sve religije jednake, da su sve od Boga u istom smislu ili da se prihvaćaju njihove molitvene formule.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska tvrdnja o jedinstvenom i univerzalnom Spasitelju ne isključuje poštovanje pripadnika drugih religija ni iskren dijalog s njima; dijalog može biti praćen jasnim svjedočenjem Kristu. Ivan Pavao II. naučavao je da samo Krist spašava, ali i da se vjernici drugih religija mogu okrenuti Bogu te primiti spasenje koje dolazi od Krista, a ne od neke neovisne spasonosne moći njihovih religija.
magisterium.assessment_en: The call for persevering prayer and fasting and the assertion that Jesus died for the whole world are in accordance with Catholic faith. However, condemnation of the spirit of Assisi as heresy and interreligious meetings as destruction of the Church is seriously unaligned with Catholic teaching and the interpretation presented by John Paul II.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Christian assertion of the unique and universal Savior does not exclude respect for members of other religions or sincere dialogue with them; dialogue can be accompanied by clear witness to Christ. John Paul II taught that only Christ saves, but also that believers of other religions can turn to God and receive the salvation that comes from Christ, and not from some independent salvific power of their religions.
concerns_en: John Paul II explicitly explained that the meeting in Assisi was not syncretism: participants prayed for peace without renouncing their different religious convictions. Therefore, calling it heresy for the people who participated or claiming that such meetings necessarily destroy the Church misrepresents its nature.

Catholic teaching simultaneously confirms that salvation is only in Christ and that the Church must proclaim Christ, while recognizing that elements of truth and goodness can exist in other religions. Respect and dialogue do not mean that all religions are equal, that all are from God in the same sense, or that their prayer formulas are accepted.

sections.subtitle_en: Fighting fire with fire: perseverance and criticism of interreligious gatherings
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar criticizes interreligious meetings for peace
sections.content_en:
Despite these fruits, evil is still powerfully present, Grebenar warns, so the community "has no other choice". **One nail drives out another / like cures like**: one must remain together in prayer and fasting. He expresses a firm conviction that the Lord, even after this podcast one day ends, will keep together the community of people gathered around prayer and fasting, always in unity with "holy mother Church".

Finally, he briefly touches upon the so-called **“spirit of Assisi”**, interreligious meetings where representatives of different religions, among them Christians, speak together about peace. Grebenar calls this a "charade" and considers that nothing comes of it. He describes it as heresy and a "dialogue with the modern world" that **destroys the Church from within**. Such gatherings, he says, tell the faithful that all religions speak of the good and that all are from God. Whoever acts like that, he claims, has not defended Christ the Lord and has debased the sacrifice on the cross.

He emphasizes that only Christians have a Savior, but that Savior did not die only for them, but for the whole world. Therefore, believers should say to Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists, and atheists: **“Jesus Christ died for you too.”**

sections.subtitle: Ovce s desna, jarci s lijeva: evanđelje o posljednjem sudu
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar čita evanđelje o Sinu Čovječjem koji dolazi u slavi i razlučuje narode
sections.content:
Nakon dužeg tumačenja Izaijina proroštva o pokrivaču koji zastire sve narode, **Vladimir Grebenar**, voditelj podcasta Ora et Labora, čita evanđeoski odlomak dana. Riječ je o jednom od najdramatičnijih prizora u Svetom pismu, o slici posljednjeg suda.

Kad Sin Čovječji dođe u slavi i svi anđeli njegovi s njime, sjest će na prijestolje slave svoje. Pred njim će se sabrati svi narodi, a on će ih razlučiti kao što pastir razlučuje ovce od jaraca: ovce sebi s desna, jarce s lijeva. Onima s desna kralj će reći: „Dođite, blagoslovljeni Oca mojega! Primite u baštinu Kraljevstvo pripravljeno za vas od postanka svijeta.“

Obrazloženje presude jednostavno je i konkretno:
- bio je gladan i dali su mu jesti,
- bio je žedan i napojili su ga,
- bio je stranac i primili su ga,
- bio je gol i zaogrnuli su ga,
- bio je bolestan i pohodili su ga,
- bio je u tamnici i došli su k njemu.

Pravednici se čude i pitaju kada su ga to vidjeli u takvom stanju. Kralj im odgovara: „Zaista, kažem vam, što god učiniste jednom od ove moje najmanje braće, meni učiniste.“ Onima s lijeva reći će: „Odlazite od mene, prokleti, u oganj vječni, pripravljen đavlu i anđelima njegovim.“ Oni su propustili činiti upravo ta djela. Odlomak završava rečenicom koja će obilježiti cijelo tumačenje: „I otići će ovi u muku vječnu, a pravednici u život vječni.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je vrlo usklađen s katoličkim naukom i vjerno prenosi Mt 25,31–46: Krist sudi svim narodima, a djela milosrđa prema potrebitima prikazana su kao djela učinjena njemu samomu. Naglasak na vječnom životu pravednika i vječnoj kazni onih koji su zanemarili milosrđe odgovara završetku evanđeoskog odlomka i katoličkom nauku o posljednjem sudu.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusova identifikacija s najmanjima pokazuje da ljubav prema Bogu nije odvojena od konkretne brige za bližnje, osobito gladne, strance, bolesne i zatvorenike. Prizor je ozbiljan poziv na obraćenje i djela milosrđa, ali ga se ne treba svesti na puko računovodstvo pojedinačnih dobrih djela: evanđelje otkriva kakav je odnos čovjek imao prema Kristu i njegovoj braći.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is highly aligned with Catholic teaching and faithfully conveys Mt 25:31–46: Christ judges all nations, and works of mercy toward the needy are presented as deeds done to himself. The emphasis on the eternal life of the righteous and eternal punishment of those who neglected mercy corresponds to the conclusion of the Gospel passage and Catholic teaching on the Last Judgment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' identification with the least shows that love for God is not separated from concrete care for one's neighbors, especially the hungry, strangers, the sick, and prisoners. The scene is a serious call to conversion and works of mercy, but it should not be reduced to mere bookkeeping of individual good deeds: the Gospel reveals what kind of relationship man had toward Christ and his brethren.

sections.subtitle_en: Sheep on the right, goats on the left: the Gospel of the Last Judgment
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar reads the Gospel of the Son of Man coming in glory and separating the nations
sections.content_en:
After a lengthy interpretation of Isaiah's prophecy about the veil that covers all peoples, **Vladimir Grebenar**, host of the podcast Ora et Labora, reads the Gospel passage of the day. It is one of the most dramatic scenes in Sacred Scripture, the image of the Last Judgment.

When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, He will sit on the throne of His glory. All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats: the sheep on His right, the goats on the left. To those on the right, the King will say: "Come, you who are blessed by my Father! Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world."

The reasoning of the judgment is simple and concrete:
- He was hungry and they gave Him to eat,
- He was thirsty and they gave Him drink,
- He was a stranger and they welcomed Him,
- He was naked and they clothed Him,
- He was sick and they visited Him,
- He was in prison and they came to Him.

The righteous are amazed and ask when they saw Him in such a state. The King replies to them: "Truly, I say to you, whatever you did for one of these least brothers of mine, you did for me." To those on the left He will say: "Depart from me, you accursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels." They failed to do precisely those deeds. The passage ends with the sentence that will characterize the entire interpretation: "And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life."

sections.subtitle: Sud nakon uskrsnuća: razdvajanje će proći i kroz hrvatski narod
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava da će na posljednjem sudu i hrvatski narod biti podijeljen na ovce i jarce
sections.content:
Vladimir Grebenar pojašnjava da evanđelje opisuje **posljednji sud**, koji dolazi nakon općeg uskrsnuća. Tada će svi ljudi uskrsnuti i svi narodi stajat će pred Isusom.

Voditelj zatim sliku primjenjuje na vlastiti narod. Poziva slušatelje da zamisle kako će i unutar hrvatskog naroda jedan dio biti odvojen među ovce, a drugi među jarce. Koliki će udio biti s koje strane, ističe, nitko ne zna.

Kao primjer navodi mogućnost da se spasi samo pet posto ljudi. U tom scenariju on sam može završiti na strani jaraca, a netko od slušatelja na strani ovaca. Takav ishod naziva tragedijom: tada je sve gotovo i, kako slikovito kaže, „nema mogućnosti za popravni“. Knjige života su napisane i sve je već rečeno i učinjeno. Čovjek tada Isusu može govoriti bilo što, ali On ga više ne želi slušati.

Grebenar podsjeća da Sveto pismo taj dan naziva **velikim i strašnim danom**.

magisterium.assessment: Tvrdnja da posljednjem sudu prethodi uskrsnuće svih mrtvih, pravednih i nepravednih, te da će pred Kristom biti okupljeni svi narodi, u skladu je s katoličkim naukom. Primjer mogućih pet posto jasno je predstavljen kao hipotetski, a izričita napomena da nitko ne zna udio spašenih sprječava da se taj broj shvati kao crkveno učenje; ipak, formulacija da Isus čovjeka više ne želi slušati može pogrešno prikazati konačnost suda kao nedostatak Kristova milosrđa.
concerns: Hipotetski udio od pet posto nije biblijsko ni crkveno utvrđeno predviđanje. Iako je u odlomku označen kao mogućnost, važno je da ga se ne shvati kao procjenu stvarnog broja spašenih.

Izraz da Isus osuđenoga „više ne želi slušati” može zvučati kao da Krist odbacuje čovjeka iz samovolje ili bez milosrđa. Katolički nauk potvrđuje ozbiljnost i konačnost suda, ali tu formulaciju treba razumjeti kao nepovratnost konačne odluke, a ne kao nijekanje Božje dobrote.
magisterium.enrichment: Katekizam izričito uči da uskrsnuće svih mrtvih prethodi posljednjem sudu te da Krist razlučuje ljude kao ovce i jarce; evanđelje pritom govori o vječnom ishodu, a ne o privremenoj kazni nakon koje bi se konačni sud mogao poništiti. Istodobno, neizvjesnost o tome tko će biti osuđen nije razlog za nagađanje o postotcima: papa Franjo predstavlja posljednji sud kao ozbiljnu stvarnost, ali i kao susret s Kristom koji može biti izvor nade i pouzdanja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The claim that the Last Judgment is preceded by the resurrection of all the dead, the righteous and the unrighteous, and that all nations will be gathered before Christ, is in accordance with Catholic teaching. The example of a possible five percent is clearly presented as hypothetical, and the explicit note that no one knows the proportion of the saved prevents that number from being understood as Church teaching; nevertheless, the formulation that Jesus no longer wants to listen to man can misrepresent the finality of the judgment as a lack of Christ's mercy.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catechism explicitly teaches that the resurrection of all the dead precedes the Last Judgment and that Christ separates people as sheep and goats; the Gospel speaks here of an eternal outcome, and not of temporary punishment after which the final judgment could be overturned. At the same time, uncertainty about who will be condemned is not a reason for speculation about percentages: Pope Francis presents the Last Judgment as a serious reality, but also as an encounter with Christ that can be a source of hope and trust.
concerns_en: The hypothetical proportion of five percent is not a biblically or ecclesiastically established prediction. Although designated in the passage as a possibility, it is important that it not be understood as an estimate of the actual number of the saved.

The expression that Jesus "no longer wants to listen" to the condemned person can sound as though Christ rejects man out of arbitrariness or without mercy. Catholic teaching confirms the gravity and finality of the judgment, but that formulation should be understood as the irreversibility of the final decision, rather than a denial of God's goodness.

sections.subtitle_en: Judgment after the resurrection: the separation will pass through the Croatian people as well
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host explains that at the Last Judgment the Croatian people will also be divided into sheep and goats
sections.content_en:
Vladimir Grebenar explains that the Gospel describes the **Last Judgment**, which comes after the general resurrection. Then all people will rise and all nations will stand before Jesus.

The host then applies the image to his own nation. He invites listeners to imagine how within the Croatian people as well one part will be separated among the sheep, and the other among the goats. What proportion will be on which side, he points out, no one knows.

As an example, he mentions the possibility that only five percent of people are saved. In that scenario, he himself could end up on the side of the goats, and one of the listeners on the side of the sheep. He calls such an outcome a tragedy: then everything is finished and, as he puts it graphically, "there is no chance for a retake". The books of life are written and everything has already been said and done. A person may say anything to Jesus then, but He no longer wants to listen.

Grebenar recalls that Sacred Scripture calls that day a **great and terrible day**.

sections.subtitle: Znoj za volanom: osobno razmatranje o danu suda
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar priča kako mu se tresu noge i kako se preznojavao u automobilu razmišljajući o sudu
sections.content:
Vladimir Grebenar u ovom dijelu otvoreno govori o vlastitom doživljaju. Kad pomisli na dan suda, priznaje, noge mu se tresu.

Opisuje nedavni događaj. Vraćao se automobilom s jednog skupa i u autu molio krunicu. Nakon molitve došla mu je misao da razmišlja o posljednjem sudu i da Gospodin želi da o tome govori. Zamislio je sebe u toj situaciji: uskrsnuo je, ide na sud i ne zna na koju će stranu biti postavljen. Počeo se, kaže, preznojavati za volanom.

Grebenar naglašava kako je riječ o neizvjesnosti u kojoj je **cijela vječnost u pitanju**. U vrlo slikovitim kontrastima opisuje dvije mogućnosti:

- **Raj**: ono što „oko nije vidjelo, uho nije čulo“. Vječni život, vječna radost i vječno jedinstvo u ljubavi. Nema bolesti, kriza ni nesreća. Uvijek je dan, a Kristova svjetlost neprestano obasjava sve.
- **Pakao**: stanje nalik zatvorenosti u mrtvačkoj škrinji iz koje se ne može izaći. Čovjek je svjestan svega, sve oko njega trune i zaudara, a bol stalno raste, cijelu vječnost.

Zaključuje da je to izbor, i ponavlja: „To je izbor.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak vjerno naglašava ozbiljnost suda, stvarnu mogućnost vječnog gubitka i nadu u vječni život, ali pojedinosti o paklu prikazuje kao da su doslovno poznate, premda katolički nauk upozorava da biblijske slike treba ispravno tumačiti. Tvrdnja da je riječ o „izboru” može biti katolički prihvatljiva ako se razumije kao slobodan odgovor na Božju milost, a ne kao da se čovjek spašava vlastitom snagom ili da Bog prestaje nuditi milost.
concerns: Slika čovjeka svjesnog svega u škrinji, truljenja i boli koja stalno raste nije utvrđen opis pakla u priloženim izvorima; ako se iznosi kao doslovna činjenica, prelazi granice onoga što se može sigurno tvrditi.
Potrebno je razlikovati slobodan ljudski odgovor od samospasenja: spasenje je Božji dar i milost, iako ljudske odluke imaju vječne posljedice.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje pakla naglašava konačno i slobodno odvajanje od Boga, izvora života i radosti, a ne tvrdnju da su sve slikovite pojedinosti o njegovim mukama doslovno opisive. Evanđelje ipak ozbiljno govori o sudu i suprotnosti između vječne kazne i vječnoga života, dok crkveno promišljanje istodobno ističe da Bog nastavlja nuditi spasonosnu milost i da Crkva ne proglašava prokletstvo nijedne konkretne osobe.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage faithfully emphasizes the seriousness of judgment, the real possibility of eternal loss, and the hope of eternal life, but it presents details about hell as if they were literally known, even though Catholic teaching warns that biblical imagery must be correctly interpreted. The claim that it is a matter of „choice” can be Catholicly acceptable if understood as a free response to God's grace, and not as if man saves himself by his own strength or that God ceases to offer grace.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of hell emphasizes the definitive and free separation from God, the source of life and joy, rather than the claim that all figurative details about its torments are literally describable. The Gospel nonetheless speaks seriously about judgment and the contrast between eternal punishment and eternal life, while ecclesial reflection simultaneously highlights that God continues to offer saving grace and that the Church does not proclaim the damnation of any specific person.
concerns_en: The image of a man aware of everything in a chest, of rotting and of pain that constantly grows, is not an established description of hell in the provided sources; if presented as a literal fact, it crosses the boundaries of what can be asserted with certainty.
It is necessary to distinguish a free human response from self-salvation: salvation is God's gift and grace, although human decisions have eternal consequences.

sections.subtitle_en: Sweat behind the wheel: personal reflection on the day of judgment
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar tells how his legs shake and how he was breaking into a sweat in the car thinking about the judgment
sections.content_en:
In this part, Vladimir Grebenar speaks openly about his own experience. When he thinks of the day of judgment, he admits, his legs shake.

He describes a recent event. He was returning by car from a gathering and praying the Rosary in the car. After the prayer, a thought came to him to think about the final judgment and that the Lord wants him to speak about it. He imagined himself in that situation: he has resurrected, he is going to judgment, and he does not know which side he will be placed on. He began, he says, to break into a sweat behind the wheel.

Grebenar emphasizes that it is about an uncertainty in which **the whole eternity is at stake**. In very vivid contrasts, he describes two possibilities:

- **Heaven**: that which "eye has not seen, ear has not heard." Eternal life, eternal joy, and eternal unity in love. There is no illness, crises, or misfortunes. It is always day, and the light of Christ constantly shines upon everything.
- **Hell**: a state akin to being enclosed in a coffin from which one cannot get out. A person is aware of everything, everything around him rots and stinks, and the pain constantly grows, for all eternity.

He concludes that it is a choice, and repeats: "It is a choice."

sections.subtitle: Sve kroz prizmu spasenja: nije dovoljno govoriti „Gospodine, Gospodine“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva slušatelje da se pokrenu i čine djela, a ne samo mole i poste
sections.content:
Iz takvog razmatranja, objašnjava Grebenar, proizlazi vrlo praktičan zaključak. Treba paziti što se govori jer će se odgovarati za svaku riječ. Još je važnije, kaže, paziti **što se sluša i čita**. Cijeli život trebalo bi prilagoditi jednom cilju, spasenju. Sve što čovjek radi trebalo bi promatrati kroz prizmu spasenja, a ne raditi tek „reda radi“.

To pitanje voditelj postavlja i sebi: je li podcast koji snima na spasenje njemu i slušateljima? Odgovara da mora biti poticajan.

Zatim ističe da je Isus Krist Gospodin, Sin Božji i jedini koji je umro na križu i dao život za spasenje ljudi. Iz toga izvodi poziv: **„Pokrenimo se!“** Nije dovoljno samo moliti i postiti. Treba činiti djela, kako bi u knjizi života bilo zapisano nešto učinjeno za Gospodina. Tko se sav zauzme za Isusa, kaže, zauzima se i za vlastito spasenje i za spasenje drugih te svjedoči za Gospodina.

Vraćajući se evanđelju, Grebenar upozorava na jedan detalj. I oni na lijevoj strani Isusa oslovljavaju s „Gospodine“, dakle i oni su bili vjernici koji su ga priznavali. Zato, podsjeća, Isus kaže da neće svaki koji govori „Gospodine, Gospodine“ ući u Kraljevstvo nebesko, nego onaj koji vrši volju Oca. Spašavaju se oni koji su „u pokretu“, koji čine.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na vršenje Očeve volje i na djela, umjesto oslanjanja samo na izgovoreno priznanje vjere, dobro je utemeljen u Isusovim riječima i prispodobi o posljednjem sudu. Ipak, govor o djelima kao zapisu za spasenje i tvrdnja da su ljudi s lijeve strane bili vjernici mogu stvoriti pogrešan dojam da se spasenje zaslužuje samostalno ili da tekst potvrđuje njihovu vjersku pripadnost.
concerns: Djela ne smiju biti predstavljena kao neovisna osnova ili cijena spasenja; katolički govor treba naznačiti da su ona odgovor na Božju milost i izraz živoga odnosa s Kristom.
To što ljudi u Mateju 25 Krista oslovljavaju s „Gospodine” ne dokazuje da su bili vjernici u smislu osobne vjere ili vjernosti; odlomak naglašava njihova djela ili propuste prema potrebitima.
magisterium.enrichment: Matej 25 povezuje sud s konkretnim djelima milosrđa prema gladnima, strancima, bolesnima i zatvorenima, dok Matej 7,21 upozorava da samo izgovaranje „Gospodine” nije dovoljno bez vršenja Očeve volje. To ne suprotstavlja djela molitvi i postu niti znači da čovjek sam sebe spašava: izbori i djela važni su unutar odgovora na Božju milost, koja čovjeku prethodi i prati ga.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to do the Father's will and to works, instead of relying solely on a spoken confession of faith, is well founded in Jesus' words and the parable of the Last Judgment. However, speaking of works as a record for salvation and claiming that the people on the left side were believers can create a false impression that salvation is earned independently or that the text confirms their religious affiliation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Matthew 25 connects judgment with concrete works of mercy toward the hungry, strangers, the sick, and prisoners, while Matthew 7:21 warns that merely saying „Lord” is not enough without doing the Father's will. This does not oppose works to prayer and fasting, nor does it mean that man saves himself: choices and works are important within the response to God's grace, which precedes and accompanies man.
concerns_en: Works must not be presented as an independent basis or the price of salvation; Catholic discourse should indicate that they are a response to God's grace and an expression of a living relationship with Christ.

The fact that the people in Matthew 25 address Christ with „Lord” does not prove that they were believers in the sense of personal faith or faithfulness; the passage emphasizes their deeds or omissions toward the needy.

sections.subtitle_en: Everything through the prism of salvation: it is not enough to say „Lord, Lord“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host invites listeners to get moving and do deeds, not just pray and fast
sections.content_en:
From such reflection, Grebenar explains, comes a very practical conclusion. One must be careful what one says because one will answer for every word. It is even more important, he says, to be careful **what one listens to and reads**. One's whole life should be adapted to a single goal, salvation. Everything a person does should be viewed through the prism of salvation, and not done merely "for the sake of order."

The host also poses this question to himself: is the podcast he is recording for his salvation and that of his listeners? He answers that it must be encouraging.

Then he points out that Jesus Christ is Lord, the Son of God, and the only one who died on the cross and gave his life for the salvation of people. From this he derives a call: **"Let us get moving!"** It is not enough merely to pray and fast. One must do deeds, so that something done for the Lord is written in the book of life. Whoever commits entirely to Jesus, he says, commits to both his own salvation and the salvation of others and witnesses for the Lord.

Returning to the Gospel, Grebenar warns of one detail. Even those on the left side address Jesus as "Lord," meaning they too were believers who acknowledged him. That is why, he recalls, Jesus says that not everyone who says "Lord, Lord" will enter the Kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of the Father. Those who are "in motion," who act, are saved.

sections.subtitle: Zlatno pravilo protiv pasivnosti i oštra kritika međureligijskih susreta
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar uspoređuje kršćansko zlatno pravilo s kineskom filozofijom
sections.content:
Grebenar dalje izlaže ono što naziva **zlatnim pravilom spasenja**: „Čini drugome što želiš da drugi tebi čini.“ Tome suprotstavlja „ljudsku mudrost“ kineske filozofije, koja kaže: „Ne čini drugome što ne želiš da drugi tebi čini.“ Takav pristup, smatra, vodi u propast jer čovjeka čini pasivnim i sklonim tome da se nikome ne zamjeri.

U istu kategoriju svrstava međureligijske susrete na kojima predstavnici raznih religija i kršćani zajedno govore o miru. Takve inicijative naziva **izdajom Isusa Krista** jer, prema njegovu tumačenju, prešućuju da je Isus Sin Božji koji je umro na križu. Da bi se s pripadnikom druge religije moglo razgovarati o miru ili s njim postiti, kaže voditelj, najprije mu treba reći da je Isus Krist Sin Božji, umro na križu za sve ljude.

Kao uporište navodi Isusov nalog: „Idite po svem svijetu, propovijedajte evanđelje.“ Tko povjeruje i pokrsti se, spasit će se, a tko ne povjeruje, bit će osuđen jer nije povjerovao u jedinorođenoga Sina Božjega. „Točka. Nema dalje“, poručuje Grebenar. To je za njega kriterij svakog razgovora.

Precizira ipak da dijalog s nekršćanima o **svjetovnim pitanjima** smatra prihvatljivim. Kao primjere navodi poduzetništvo te izradu zakona, akata i uredbi. Kad je riječ o pitanjima vjere, svi se moraju prilagoditi jer je pisano: „Svaki će jezik priznati: Isus Krist jest Gospodin, na slavu Boga Oca.“ To prema njegovu tumačenju ne znači da će svaki čovjek to priznati, nego da će u svakom narodu barem jedna osoba izgovoriti to ispovijedanje.

magisterium.assessment: Ispravno je naglasiti da je Krist jedini Spasitelj te da kršćani imaju poslanje naviještati Evanđelje, ali odlomak pogrešno prikazuje međureligijski dijalog kao izdaju Krista i tvrdnju iz Fil 2,11 kao ispovijedanje samo jedne osobe u svakom narodu. Crkva uči da su dijalog i naviještanje različiti, ali povezani dijelovi evangelizacijskog poslanja, te da se vjera svjedoči uz poštovanje drugih, a ne da se suradnja za mir unaprijed proglasi nelojalnošću Kristu.
concerns: Tvrdnja da negativno oblikovano pravilo „Ne čini drugome što ne želiš da drugi tebi čini” vodi u propast nije opravdana: Ivan Pavao II. prepoznaje zlatno pravilo u različitim religijama kao dragocjeno moralno vodilo, vaikka ističe da ljubav prema bližnjemu ide dalje.

Međureligijski susreti i zajedničko zalaganje za mir nisu sami po sebi izdaja Krista. Crkveno učiteljstvo potvrđuje da dijalog ne zamjenjuje naviještanje, nego ga prati; u susretima kršćani trebaju svjedočiti Kristu, uz slušanje, poštovanje slobode i traženje dobra koje je prisutno kod drugih.

„Točka. Nema dalje” zanemaruje da se spasenje uvijek ostvaruje po Kristu, ali da Bog može spasiti i osobe koje nisu primile navještaj Evanđelja, po Kristovoj milosti i na način koji je Crkvi tajanstven. Stoga se riječi o osudi onoga tko ne vjeruje ne mogu nekritički primijeniti na svakoga tko nije izričito ispovjedio vjeru, ne uzimajući u obzir je li mu Evanđelje naviješteno i kako je na milost odgovorio.

Fil 2,11 govori o tome da će svaki jezik priznati Isusa Krista Gospodinom; tekst ne kaže da će to učiniti samo jedna osoba u svakom narodu. Tumačenje voditelja zato ne slijedi značenje citiranog stiha.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko shvaćanje drži zajedno dvije istine: Krist je jedini Spasitelj svih ljudi, a međureligijski dijalog može biti autentičan dio poslanja Crkve, a ne odustajanje od Krista. Dijalog ne zahtijeva da kršćanin prikriva svoju vjeru; traži iskreno svjedočenje i poštovanje sugovornika, dok naviještanje i dijalog ostaju povezani, ali nisu istoznačni.

magisterium.assessment_en: It is correct to emphasize that Christ is the only Savior and that Christians have a mission to proclaim the Gospel, but the passage incorrectly portrays interreligious dialogue as a betrayal of Christ and the assertion from Phil 2:11 as the confession of only one person in every nation. The Church teaches that dialogue and proclamation are distinct but connected parts of the evangelizing mission, and that faith is witnessed with respect for others, rather than cooperation for peace being declared in advance as disloyalty to Christ.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic understanding holds together two truths: Christ is the only Savior of all people, and interreligious dialogue can be an authentic part of the Church's mission, not an abandonment of Christ. Dialogue does not require a Christian to conceal his faith; it demands sincere witnessing and respect for the interlocutor, while proclamation and dialogue remain connected, but are not synonymous.
concerns_en: The claim that the negatively phrased rule „Do not do to another what you do not want another to do to you” leads to ruin is unjustified: John Paul II recognizes the Golden Rule in various religions as a precious moral guide, although pointing out that love of neighbor goes further.

Interreligious gatherings and joint efforts for peace are not in themselves a betrayal of Christ. The Church's Magisterium confirms that dialogue does not replace proclamation, but accompanies it; in encounters, Christians should bear witness to Christ, alongside listening, respecting freedom, and seeking the good that is present among others.

„Period. That's it” ignores that salvation is always realized through Christ, but that God can also save persons who have not received the proclamation of the Gospel, through Christ's grace and in a manner that is mysterious to the Church. Therefore, the words concerning the condemnation of whoever does not believe cannot be uncritically applied to everyone who has not explicitly confessed the faith, without considering whether the Gospel was proclaimed to him and how he responded to grace.

Phil 2:11 speaks of every tongue confessing Jesus Christ as Lord; the text does not say that only one person in every nation will do so. The host's interpretation therefore does not follow the meaning of the quoted verse.

sections.subtitle_en: The Golden Rule against passivity and sharp criticism of interreligious meetings
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar compares the Christian Golden Rule with Chinese philosophy
sections.content_en:
Grebenar further expounds what he calls the **Golden Rule of salvation**: "Do to another what you want another to do to you." To this he contrasts the "human wisdom" of Chinese philosophy, which says: "Do not do to another what you do not want another to do to you." Such an approach, he believes, leads to ruin because it makes a person passive and prone to not offending anyone.

Into the same category he places interreligious meetings where representatives of various religions and Christians speak together about peace. He calls such initiatives a **betrayal of Jesus Christ** because, according to his interpretation, they keep silent about Jesus being the Son of God who died on the cross. In order to be able to speak about peace with a member of another religion or fast with him, says the host, one must first tell him that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, who died on the cross for all people.

As a foundation he cites Jesus's mandate: "Go into all the world, proclaim the Gospel." Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned because he did not believe in the only-begotten Son of God. "Period. Nothing beyond that," says Grebenar. That is for him the criterion of every conversation.

He specifies, however, that he considers dialogue with non-Christians on **secular matters** acceptable. As examples, he cites entrepreneurship and the drafting of laws, acts, and regulations. When it comes to matters of faith, everyone must conform because it is written: "Every tongue will confess: Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father." According to his interpretation, this does not mean that every person will confess it, but that in every nation at least one person will utter that confession.

sections.subtitle: Jedan pravednik dovoljan je Bogu: od Joba i Noe do Krista
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj navodi primjer Joba kojeg Bog ističe pred Sotonom

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno ispovijeda da je Krist jedini Spasitelj i može opravdano prikazati Adama i Krista kao važne glave čovječanstva, ali primjeri Joba i Noe ne dokazuju da je Bogu dostatna samo jedna osoba koja ga ispovijeda u svakom narodu. Tvrdnja o „prvom spominjanju Sotone” nije potkrijepljena dostupnim izvorima, pa se njezina točnost ovdje ne može potvrditi.
concerns: Biblijski primjeri pojedinaca koje Bog posebno ističe ne uspostavljaju sami po sebi pravilo da je dovoljan jedan ispovjednik vjere po narodu; takav zaključak nadilazi ono što je navedeno u odlomku.

Usporedba Adama, Noe i Krista može imati ilustrativnu snagu, ali ne smije prikriti bitnu razliku: Adam je u kršćanskoj teologiji praotac čovječanstva, dok je Krist jedini Spasitelj; Kristova jedinstvena uloga ne proizlazi iz toga što je samo „jedan čovjek”.
Dostupni izvori ne potvrđuju tvrdnju da je Job prvi spomen Sotone u Svetom pismu, niti pružaju dovoljno podloge za ocjenu tog detalja.
magisterium.enrichment: U kršćanskom tumačenju Adam i Krist mogu se usporediti kao predstavnici dvaju načina odnosa čovječanstva prema grijehu i životu: izvor navodi da se Krist naziva „posljednjim Adamom” te ističe da je spasenje svih ljudi poziv na sudjelovanje u njegovu spasenju. To ne znači da Adam, Noa i Krist imaju jednaku spasenjsku ulogu: spasenje dolazi jedino po Kristu, premda se njegova milost može odnositi i na one koji ga ne poznaju izričito.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly confesses that Christ is the only Savior and can legitimately present Adam and Christ as important heads of humanity, but the examples of Job and Noah do not prove that for God only one person who confesses him in each nation is sufficient. The claim about the „first mention of Satan” is not substantiated by the available sources, so its accuracy cannot be confirmed here.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Christian interpretation, Adam and Christ can be compared as representatives of two ways of humanity's relationship toward sin and life: the source notes that Christ is called the „last Adam” and emphasizes that the salvation of all people is a call to participate in his salvation. This does not mean that Adam, Noah, and Christ have an equal salvific role: salvation comes solely through Christ, although his grace can also apply to those who do not explicitly know him.
concerns_en: Biblical examples of individuals whom God specially highlights do not in themselves establish a rule that one confessor of the faith per nation is sufficient; such a conclusion goes beyond what is stated in the passage.

The comparison of Adam, Noah, and Christ may have illustrative power, but it must not obscure the essential difference: in Christian theology Adam is the forefather of humanity, while Christ is the only Savior; Christ's unique role does not stem from being merely „one man”.
Available sources do not confirm the claim that Job is the first mention of Satan in Sacred Scripture, nor do they provide sufficient basis for assessing that detail.
